article: Pedestrians in videos have a wide range of appearances such as body poses, occlusions, and complex backgrounds, and there exists the proposal shift problem in pedestrian detection that causes the loss of body parts such as head and legs. To address it, we propose part-level convolutional neural networks (CNN) for pedestrian detection using saliency and boundary box alignment in this paper. The proposed network consists of two sub-networks: detection and alignment. We use saliency in the detection sub-network to remove false positives such as lamp posts and trees. We adopt bounding box alignment on detection proposals in the alignment sub-network to address the proposal shift problem. First, we combine FCN and CAM to extract deep features for pedestrian detection. Then, we perform part-level CNN to recall the lost body parts. Experimental results on various datasets demonstrate that the proposed method remarkably improves accuracy in pedestrian detection and outperforms existing state-of-the-arts in terms of log average miss rate at false position per image (FPPI).

article: We develop a probabilistic framework for deep learning based on the Deep Rendering Mixture Model (DRMM), a new generative probabilistic model that explicitly capture variations in data due to latent factors. DRMM allows for flexible and efficient inference and learning algorithms, enabling us to train deep models that can make accurate predictions even in the presence of missing or corrupted data. By incorporating prior knowledge about the underlying factors of variation in the data, DRMM can greatly improve the accuracy and robustness of deep learning models. This approach has many potential applications in fields such as computer vision, natural language processing, and speech recognition, and we are excited to continue exploring its capabilities.
label: machine

article: This paper presents an evaluation of a number of probabilistic algorithms for localization of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) using bathymetry data. The algorithms, based on the principles of the Bayes filter, work by fusing bathymetry information with depth and altitude data from an AUV. Four different Bayes filter-based algorithms are used to design the localization algorithms: the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF), Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF), Particle Filter (PF), and Marginalized Particle Filter (MPF). We evaluate the performance of these four Bayesian bathymetry-based AUV localization approaches under variable conditions and available computational resources. The localization algorithms overcome unique challenges of the underwater domain, including visual distortion and radio frequency (RF) signal attenuation, which often make landmark-based localization infeasible. Evaluation results on real-world bathymetric data show the effectiveness of each algorithm under a variety of conditions, with the MPF being the most accurate.

article: Structured illumination microscopy (SIM) is a very important super-resolution microscopy technique, which provides high speed super-resolution with about two-fold spatial resolution enhancement. Several attempts aimed at improving the performance of SIM reconstruction algorithm have been reported. However, most of these highlight only one specific aspect of the SIM reconstruction - such as the determination of the illumination pattern phase shift accurately - whereas other key elements - such as determination of modulation factor, estimation of object power spectrum, Wiener filtering frequency components with inclusion of object power spectrum information, translocating and the merging of the overlapping frequency components - are usually glossed over superficially. In addition, most of the work reported lie scattered throughout the literature and a comprehensive review of the theoretical background is found lacking. The purpose of the present work is two-fold: 1) to collect the essential theoretical details of SIM algorithm at one place, thereby making them readily accessible to readers for the first time; and 2) to provide an open source SIM reconstruction code (named OpenSIM), which enables users to interactively vary the code parameters and study it's effect on reconstructed SIM image.
label: human

article: The creation and support of Embodied Conversational Agents (ECAs) has been quite challenging, as features required might not be straight-forward to implement and to integrate in a single application. Furthermore, ECAs as desktop applications present drawbacks for both developers and users; the former have to develop for each device and operating system and the latter must install additional software, limiting their widespread use. In this paper we demonstrate how recent advances in web technologies show promising steps towards capable web-based ECAs, through some off-the-shelf technologies, in particular, the Web Speech API, Web Audio API, WebGL and Web Workers. We describe their integration into a simple fully functional web-based 3D ECA accessible from any modern device, with special attention to our novel work in the creation and support of the embodiment aspects.
label: human

article: We construct Global Voices , a multilingual dataset for evaluating cross-lingual summarization methods. We extract social-network descriptions of Global Voices news articles to cheaply collect evaluation data for into-English and from-English summarization in 15 languages. Especially, for the into-English summarization task, we crowd-source a high-quality evaluation dataset based on guidelines that emphasize accuracy, coverage, and understandability. To ensure the quality of this dataset, we collect human ratings to filter out bad summaries, and conduct a survey on humans, which shows that the remaining summaries are preferred over the social-network summaries. We study the effect of translation quality in cross-lingual summarization, comparing a translate-then-summarize approach with several baselines. Our results highlight the limitations of the Rouge metric that are overlooked in monolingual summarization. Our dataset is available for download at .
label: human

article: Real-world audio recordings are often degraded by factors such as noise, reverberation, and equalization distortion. This paper introduces HiFi-GAN, a deep learning method to transform recorded speech to sound as if it were recorded with high-fidelity equipment in a studio environment. HiFi-GAN is trained using adversarial loss and feature matching loss to improve the perceptual quality of the generated audio. The architecture of HiFi-GAN consists of a generator network and a discriminator network. The generator network is a deep convolutional neural network that learns to generate high-fidelity audio from degraded input. The discriminator network is also a deep convolutional neural network that learns to distinguish between real high-fidelity audio and generated audio. The generator network takes a degraded audio signal as input and generates a high-fidelity audio signal as output. The discriminator network then evaluates the quality of the generated audio signal and reports its output to the generator network. The generator network adjusts its output to improve its performance by minimizing the error between the output of the discriminator network and the generated audio signal. Experimental results show that HiFi-GAN outperforms other state-of-the-art methods in terms of speech enhancement and audio quality. HiFi-GAN also outperforms other methods in terms of stability and robustness. This makes it a useful tool in a variety of audio processing applications, including speech recognition, audio restoration, and music analysis.
label: machine

article: We propose a benchmarking strategy that is robust in the presence of timer error, OS jitter and other environmental fluctuations, and is insensitive to the highly nonideal statistics produced by such fluctuations. To implement a robust benchmarking strategy, we recommend the following steps: 1. Choose a representative workload: Select a workload that represents the typical usage scenario for your systemapplication. A representative workload should entail a mix of compute, memory, storage, and network-intensive tasks. 2. Conduct a warm-up period: Before starting the benchmarking, allow the systemapplication to run for some time, so that it can reach its steady state. Running the workload for a few minutes will ensure that the system has completed all the initialization and has reached its optimal state. 3. Measure the baseline performance: Run the workload several times to measure the baseline performance. The baseline performance gives an idea of the system's maximum and minimum performance limits. 4. Randomize the run-order: To eliminate the effects of the timer error and other environmental fluctuations, it is recommended to randomize the order of the runs. Each run should be assigned a random sequence number to achieve a uniformly distributed order. 5. Use statistical tools: Due to the highly nonideal statistics produced by the fluctuations, it may not always be possible to obtain a clear picture of system behavior. Hence, using statistical tools like standard deviation, variance, and coefficient of variation can help make sense of the data. 6. Validate the results: After completing the benchmarking, ensure that the results are accurate and validated. Repeating the experiments on different systems can help validate the results. By following the above steps, you can implement a robust benchmarking strategy that can account for timer error, OS jitter, and other environmental fluctuations while ensuring accurate, validated results.
label: machine

article: In this work we introduce a differential rendering module which allows neural networks to efficiently process cluttered data. The module is composed of continuous piecewise differentiable functions defined as a hierarchical set of 2D grids, and it enables the network to focus on important regions of the input data while ignoring irrelevant ones. This is particularly useful in scenarios where the data is inherently high-dimensional, such as in computer vision applications. Additionally, the differential rendering module provides a way to incorporate prior knowledge about the data in the form of constraints on the function parameters. This can lead to improved performance and generalization of the network. Overall, the differential rendering module is a valuable tool for deep learning practitioners who want to tackle complex real-world problems where the data is noisy, cluttered or otherwise difficult to process.
label: machine

article: We prove that octants are cover-decomposable into multiple coverings, i.e., for any k there is an m (k) such that any m (k) -fold covering of any subset of the octant can be decomposed into a finite number of disjoint k-fold coverings. To start, let's define an octant. An octant is a region of space that is bounded by three perpendicular planes. It is defined by a set of eight points that are the vertices of a cube. Now, let's consider a subset of the octant. We want to show that any k-fold covering of this subset can be decomposed into a finite number of disjoint k-fold coverings. To do this, we will use a constructive proof. We will first prove that any 2-fold covering can be decomposed into a finite number of disjoint 2-fold coverings. Then, we will use this result to prove that any k-fold covering can be decomposed into a finite number of disjoint k-fold coverings. Let's start with the case of 2-fold coverings. Consider a subset of the octant that is covered by two overlapping regions. We can decompose this 2-fold covering into three disjoint 2-fold coverings as follows: 1. The region that is covered by both coverings 2. The region that is covered only by the first covering 3. The region that is covered only by the second covering By definition, these three regions are disjoint, and together they cover the original subset. Using this result, we can now prove that any k-fold covering can be decomposed into a finite number of disjoint k-fold coverings. Consider a subset of the octant that is covered by k overlapping regions. We can decompose this k-fold covering into a finite number of disjoint 2-fold coverings as follows: 1. Choose any two overlapping regions and decompose them into three disjoint 2-fold coverings using the method described above. 2. We now have k-1 regions left to cover. Repeat the process with any two overlapping regions until we have decomposed the k-fold covering into a finite number of disjoint 2-fold coverings. Since each 2-fold covering can be decomposed into a finite number of disjoint 2-fold coverings, and we only need to repeat this process a finite number of times, we have shown that any k-fold covering can be decomposed into a finite number of disjoint k-fold coverings. Thus, we have proved that octants are cover-decomposable into multiple coverings.
label: machine

article: Variational Bayes (VB) is a recent approximate method for Bayesian inference. It has the merit of being a fast and scalable alternative to Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) but its approximation error is often unknown. However, this process can be very inefficient for large lists, especially if we need to find the rank of multiple elements. A more efficient approach involves using a divide-and-conquer algorithm, such as binary search. This algorithm works by repeatedly dividing the list in half and comparing the target element with the midpoint of the current sub-list. If the target element is smaller than the midpoint, we discard the right half of the sub-list and continue the search on the left half. Similarly, if the target element is larger than the midpoint, we discard the left half and continue the search on the right half. We repeat this process until we find the target element or determine that it is not in the list. To find the rank of an element using binary search, we can modify the standard algorithm to keep track of the number of elements we discard at each step. When we finally find the target element, the rank of the element is simply the sum of the number of elements we skipped over plus one (since we start counting from 1). OPDAS utilizes the primal-dual approach to optimize the allocation of resources to jobs while minimizing the cost function. The paper also provides an extensive analysis of the performance of OPDAS against other existing algorithms on synthetic and real-world datasets. The results show that OPDAS outperforms other algorithms in terms of average job completion time, resource utilization, and the number of jobs completed within their deadlines. Overall, the paper provides a valuable contribution in solving an important problem in cloud computing and resource allocation. The proposed OPDAS algorithm has practical applications and can lead to improvements in the efficiency and profitability of cloud-based services.

article: This paper presents the link availability probability. We evaluate and compare the link availability probability for routing protocols; Ad hoc On-demand Distance vector (AODV), Dynamic Source Routing (DSR) and Fisheye Routing Protocol (FSR) in a mobile ad hoc network (MANET) environment. The link availability probability is defined as the probability that a link between two nodes in the network remains operational for a certain amount of time. To evaluate the link availability probability, we conducted simulations using the Network Simulator 2 (NS-2) tool. We used different mobility models and node densities to simulate various scenarios in the MANET environment. The simulation results showed that FSR outperformed AODV and DSR in terms of the link availability probability. Particularly, FSR showed a significant improvement in the link availability probability with increasing node densities. In conclusion, the link availability probability is an important metric that can be used to evaluate the performance of routing protocols in a MANET environment. The simulation results presented in this paper demonstrate that FSR is a promising routing protocol for improving link availability in MANETs.

article: Under successive cancellation (SC) decoding, polar codes are inferior to other codes of similar blocklength in terms of frame error rate. While more sophisticated decoding algorithms such as list- or belief propagation (BP) decoding can significantly improve the performance of polar codes and bring them close to the performance of other state-of-the-art codes, they come at the cost of increased complexity. However, polar codes have several advantages over other codes. One of the main advantages is their low encoding complexity, which is linear in the block length. They also have a systematic structure, which means that the original data is preserved in the codeword. This makes them ideal for applications where reliability and security are vital, such as 5G communication systems, where polar codes are used for channel coding. Overall, while polar codes may not be the best choice for all communication scenarios, they offer a good balance between performance, complexity, and reliability in certain applications, making them a popular choice for modern communication systems.

article: Flow-based generative models have become an important class of unsupervised learning approaches. We demonstrate our method mainly on the CelebA dataset and show that the disentangled representations at different scales enable semantic manipulation and style mixing of the images. To visualize the latent representations, we introduce receptive fields for flow-based models and find that the receptive fields learned by RG-Flow are similar to those in convolutional neural networks. In addition, we replace the widely adopted Gaussian prior distribution by a sparse prior distribution to further enhance the disentanglement of representations. From a theoretical perspective, the proposed method has O (log L) complexity for image inpainting compared to previous generative models with O (L 2) complexity.

article: In anonymous broadcast, one or more parties want to anonymously send messages to all parties. This problem is increasingly important as a black-box in many privacy-preserving applications such as anonymous communication, distributed auctions, and multi-party computation. In this paper, we design decentralized protocols for anonymous broadcast that require each party to send (and compute) a polylogarithmic number of bits (and operations) per anonymous bit delivered with O (log n) rounds of communication. Our protocol is provably secure against traffic analysis, does not require any trusted party, and is completely load-balanced. The protocol tolerates up to n 6 statically-scheduled Byzantine parties that are controlled by a computationally unbounded adversary. Our main strategy for achieving scalability is to perform local communications (and computations) among a logarithmic number of parties. We provide simulation results to show that our protocol improves significantly over previous work. We finally show that using a common cryptographic tool in our protocol one can achieve practical results for anonymous broadcast.

article: Current neural network-based conversational models lack diversity and generate boring responses to open-ended utterances. Priors such as persona, emotion, or topic provide additional information to dialog models to aid response generation, but they still can become repetitive and predictable. There are various ways to enhance the diversity of generated responses, such as incorporating external knowledge sources or injecting randomness in the generation process. One approach is to use reinforcement learning techniques to encourage the model to explore different ways of responding. By providing rewards for generating diverse and interesting responses, the model can learn to avoid the repetitive patterns and explore new ways of conversation. Another approach is to use adversarial training, where a discriminator is trained to distinguish between real and generated responses. The generator is then trained to produce responses that not only fool the discriminator but also diversify the generated responses. Overall, the key to generating diverse and engaging responses is to incorporate creativity and exploration into the modelling process. By allowing the model to take risks and experiment with novel ways of responding, we can create more interesting and personalized conversations.

article: K-Medoids (KM) is a standard clustering method, used extensively on semi-metric data. Error analyses of KM have traditionally used an in-sample notion of error, which can be far from the actual error on out-of-sample data. To address this issue, researchers have proposed using cross-validation techniques to estimate the true error of KM on unseen data. One common cross-validation approach for KM is the leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) method. LOOCV involves removing one data point at a time from the dataset and clustering the remaining data using KM. The removed data point is then assigned to the cluster that has the closest medoid. This process is repeated for all data points, and the clusters obtained are compared to the true clusters to calculate the error. Another cross-validation approach for KM is k-fold cross-validation (KFCV), which involves dividing the data into k subsets or folds. One fold is used as the validation set, and the remaining folds are used for training. The KM algorithm is applied to the training set, and the resulting clusters are used to predict the clusters of the validation set. This process is repeated k times, with each fold used as the validation set once. The error is then calculated based on the predictions made for the validation sets. Both LOOCV and KFCV can provide a more accurate estimate of the true error of KM on new data than in-sample error measures, such as the sum of squared distances between data points and their medoids. However, these methods can be computationally expensive, especially for large datasets, and may not be necessary for simpler datasets.

article: Introducing factors, that is to say, word features such as linguistic information referring to the source tokens, is known to improve the results of neural machine translation systems in certain scenarios. Additionally, factors can also help to address common translation challenges such as word sense disambiguation and handling different word orders. However, it is important to note that incorporating factors can also increase the complexity of the model, which can impact training time and performance. Therefore, it is important to carefully evaluate the benefits and drawbacks of using factors in a given scenario before incorporating them into a neural machine translation system.

article: This paper deals with motion capture of kinematic chains (e.g. human skeletons) from monocular image sequences taken by uncalibrated cameras. An optimization of the nuclear norm is proposed that implicitly enforces structural properties of the kinematic chain. Unlike other approaches our method does not require specific camera or object motion and is not relying on training data or previously determined constraints such as particular body lengths. The proposed algorithm is able to reconstruct scenes with limited camera motion and previously unseen motions. It is not only applicable to human skeletons but also to other kinematic chains for instance animals or industrial robots. article: Federated learning has received great attention for its capability to train a large-scale model in a decentralized manner without needing to access user data directly. Existing federated learning approaches usually adopt a single global model to capture the shared knowledge of all users by aggregating their gradients, regardless of the discrepancy between their data distributions. However, due to the diverse nature of user behaviors, assigning users' gradients to different global models (i.e., centers) can better capture the heterogeneity of data distributions across users. Our paper proposes a novel multi-center aggregation mechanism for federated learning, which learns multiple global models from the non-IID user data and simultaneously derives the optimal matching between users and centers. We formulate the problem as a joint optimization that can be efficiently solved by a stochastic expectation maximization (EM) algorithm. Our experimental results on benchmark datasets show that our method outperforms several popular federated learning methods.

article: In this paper, a new graph partitioning problem is introduced. The depth of each part is constrained, i.e., the node count in the longest path of the corresponding sub-graph is no more than a predetermined positive integer value p. An additional constraint is enforced such that each part contains only nodes selected from consecutive levels in the graph. The problem is therefore transformed into a Depth-bounded Levelized Graph Partitioning (DLGP) problem, which is solved optimally using a dynamic programming algorithm. As an example application, we have shown that DLGP can effectively generate timing-correct circuit solutions for Single Flux Quantum (SFQ) logic, which is a magnetic-pulse-based, gate-level pipelined superconductive computing fabric. Experimental results confirm that DLGP generates circuits with considerably lower path balancing overheads compared with a baseline full-path-balancing approach. For example, the balancing overhead (a critical measure of quality metric) for the SFQ circuit realization in terms of D-Flip-Flop count is reduced by 3.61 x on average for 10 benchmark circuit, given p 5.

article: Recognizing multiple labels of images is a fundamental but challenging task in computer vision, and remarkable progress has been attained by localizing semantic-aware image regions and predicting their labels with deep learning models such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs). Some popular approaches for multi-label image recognition include: 1. Binary Relevance: This approach treats each label as a separate binary classification problem. This means that for each label, one classifier is trained to predict whether or not the label is present in the image. This method is simple and easy to implement, but it does not consider any correlations between the labels. 2. Label Powerset: This approach transforms the multi-label problem into a multi-class problem by combining all possible label combinations. Each unique combination is treated as a class, and a classifier is trained to predict which combination of labels is present in the image. This method considers correlations between labels, but it requires training a large number of classifiers, which can lead to computational complexity. 3. Classifier Chains: This approach attempts to capture the correlations between labels by sequentially training classifiers for each label in a specific order. Each classifier uses the predicted labels of the previous classifiers as additional features. This method considers correlations between labels, and it requires fewer classifiers than the Label Powerset method. 4. Multi-Label k-Nearest Neighbors (MLkNN): This non-parametric method is based on k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) and extends it to the multi-label case. It models the conditional probability of each label given the image features using k-NN neighbors. This method can handle imbalanced datasets and requires no training time, but it can be computationally expensive during testing. There are many other approaches for multi-label image recognition, and the choice of method depends on various factors such as dataset size, label correlations, computational resources, and performance metrics.

article: Following each patient visit, physicians must draft detailed clinical summaries called SOAP notes. Moreover, with electronic health records, these notes must be digitized. In a parallel development, patients increasingly record audio from their visits (with consent), often through dedicated apps. In this paper, we present the first study to evaluate complete pipelines for leveraging these transcripts to train machine learning model to generate these notes. We first describe a unique dataset of patient visit records, consisting of transcripts, paired SOAP notes, and annotations marking noteworthy utterances that support each summary sentence. We decompose the problem into extractive and abstractive subtasks, exploring a spectrum of approaches according to how much they demand from each component. Our best performing method first (i) extracts noteworthy utterances via multi-label classification assigns them to summary section (s); (ii) clusters noteworthy utterances on a per-section basis; and (iii) generates the summary sentences by conditioning on the corresponding cluster and the subsection of the SOAP sentence to be generated. Compared to an end-to-end approach that generates the full SOAP note from the full conversation, our approach improves by 7 ROUGE-1 points. Oracle experiments indicate that fixing our generative capabilities, improvements in extraction alone could provide (up to) a further 9 ROUGE point gain.

article: Consider a collaborative task carried out by two autonomous agents that can communicate over a noisy channel. Each agent is only aware of its own state, while the accomplishment of the task depends on the joint behavior and coordination of both agents. In such a scenario, the communication channel becomes a critical factor in the performance of the task. The agents need to be able to effectively transmit and receive information from one another despite the noise in the channel. To mitigate the effects of noise and ensure efficient communication, the agents can use coding schemes, such as error-correcting codes or error-detecting codes, to improve the reliability of the message transmission. They can also use protocols for message exchange, such as acknowledgment-based protocols, to guarantee that messages are received by the intended recipient. In addition to communication strategies, the agents can also use coordination and decision-making algorithms to perform the task collaboratively. Examples of such algorithms include consensus algorithms, where the agents converge to a common decision or action, and distributed optimization algorithms, where the agents optimize a shared objective function while taking into account the constraints and preferences of both agents. Overall, successful collaboration between two autonomous agents depends on both effective communication and coordinated decision-making. Strategies, algorithms, and protocols that enable reliable and efficient communication can help ensure the successful completion of the task at hand.

article: We study the problem of maximizing a monotone set function subject to a cardinality constraint k in the setting where some number of elements is deleted from the returned set. The focus of this work is on the worst-case adversarial setting. While there exist constant-factor guarantees when the function is submodular , there are no guarantees for non-submodular objectives. In this work, we present a new algorithm Oblivious-Greedy and prove the first constant-factor approximation guarantees for a wider class of non-submodular objectives. The obtained theoretical bounds are the first constant-factor bounds that also hold in the linear regime , i.e. when the number of deletions is linear in k . Our bounds depend on established parameters such as the submodularity ratio and some novel ones such as the inverse curvature . We bound these parameters for two important objectives including support selection and variance reduction. Finally, we numerically demonstrate the robust performance of Oblivious-Greedy for these two objectives on various datasets.

These challenges have led to the development of new optimization and regularization techniques, such as batch normalization and adaptive learning rate methods, to help improve the training of deep neural networks.

article: This paper presents eight PAC-Bayes bounds to analyze the generalization performance of multi-view classifiers. The PAC-Bayesian framework enables us to derive bounds on the expected generalization error of multi-view classifiers by leveraging the information provided by the data and the priors. These bounds have been evaluated on various datasets and compared against state-of-the-art alternatives, showing their effectiveness in providing tighter generalization error estimates and improving the overall accuracy of multi-view classifiers. Overall, this paper provides a valuable contribution to the field of multi-view learning and can facilitate the development of more robust and accurate multi-view classification models.

article: Our premise is that autonomous vehicles must optimize communications and motion planning jointly. The goal is to optimize the driving utility of the autonomous vehicle. We apply the Q-learning algorithm to make the vehicle learn the optimal policy, which makes the optimal choice of planning and communications actions at any given time. article: Deep neural networks have made breakthroughs in a wide range of visual understanding tasks. A typical challenge that hinders their real-world applications is that unknown samples may be fed into the system during the testing phase, but traditional deep neural networks will wrongly recognize these unknown samples as one of the known classes. Open set recognition (OSR) is a potential solution to overcome this problem, where the open set classifier should have the flexibility to reject unknown samples and meanwhile maintain high classification accuracy in known classes. Probabilistic generative models, such as Variational Autoencoders (VAE) and Adversarial Autoencoders (AAE), are popular methods to detect unknowns, but they cannot provide discriminative representations for known classification. In this paper, we propose a novel framework, called Conditional Probabilistic Generative Models (CPGM), for open set recognition. The core insight of our work is to add discriminative information into the probabilistic generative models, such that the proposed models can not only detect unknown samples but also classify known classes by forcing different latent features to approximate conditional Gaussian distributions. We discuss many model variants and provide comprehensive experiments to study their characteristics. Experiment results on multiple benchmark datasets reveal that the proposed method significantly outperforms the baselines and achieves new state-of-the-art performance.

article: The main limitation of visible light communication (VLC) is the narrow modulation bandwidth, which reduces the achievable data rates. Our results indicate that GRPA significantly enhances system performance compared to the static power allocation. We also study the effect of tuning the transmission angles of the light emitting diodes (LEDs) and the field of views (FOVs) of the receivers, and demonstrate that these parameters can offer new degrees of freedom to boost NOMA performance. Simulation results reveal that NOMA is a promising multiple access scheme for the downlink of VLC networks.

article: Hybrid testing combines fuzz testing and concolic execution. It leverages fuzz testing to test easy-to-reach code regions and uses concolic execution to explore code blocks guarded by complex branch conditions. As a result, hybrid testing is able to reach deeper into program state space than fuzz testing or concolic execution alone. Recently, hybrid testing has seen significant advancement. However, its code coverage-centric design is inefficient in vulnerability detection. First, it blindly selects seeds for concolic execution and aims to explore new code continuously. However, as statistics show, a large portion of the explored code is often bug-free. Therefore, giving equal attention to every part of the code during hybrid testing is a non-optimal strategy. It slows down the detection of real vulnerabilities by over 43 . Second, classic hybrid testing quickly moves on after reaching a chunk of code, rather than examining the hidden defects inside. It may frequently miss subtle vulnerabilities despite that it has already explored the vulnerable code paths. We propose SAVIOR , a new hybrid testing framework pioneering a bug-driven principle. Unlike the existing hybrid testing tools, SAVIOR prioritizes the concolic execution of the seeds that are likely to uncover more vulnerabilities. Moreover, SAVIOR verifies all vulnerable program locations along the executing program path. By modeling faulty situations using SMT constraints, SAVIOR reasons the feasibility of vulnerabilities and generates concrete test cases as proofs. Our evaluation shows that the bug-driven approach outperforms mainstream automated testing techniques, including state-of-the-art hybrid testing systems driven by code coverage. On average, SAVIOR detects vulnerabilities 43.4 faster than Driller and 44.3 faster than QSYM , leading to the discovery of 88 and 76 more unique bugs, respectively. According to the evaluation on 11 well fuzzed benchmark programs, within the first 24 hours, SAVIOR triggers 481 UBSAN violations, among which 243 are real bugs.

article: Nonlocal operators of fractional type are a popular modeling choice for applications that do not adhere to classical diffusive behavior; however, one major challenge in nonlocal simulations is the selection of an appropriate spatial kernel function for the nonlocal operator. The kernel function describes the long-range interactions between particles and influences the type of behavior that the nonlocal operator exhibits. Different applications may require different kernel functions depending on the underlying physics. Some commonly used kernel functions include the Gaussian kernel, power-law kernel, and exponential kernel. Each kernel function has its unique properties and can be chosen based on the specific application. For example, the Gaussian kernel is often used for diffusion processes, while the power-law kernel is relevant for scale-free systems that exhibit power-law behavior. In addition to the choice of kernel function, the choice of the domain over which the nonlocal operator is defined and its associated boundary conditions can also affect the behavior of the simulations. The choice of domain and boundary conditions can vary depending on the specific problem being modeled. Overall, selecting an appropriate kernel function and domain for nonlocal simulations is crucial for accurately modeling the underlying physics of a system.

article: We define and analyze the notion of variational Wardrop equilibrium for nonatomic aggregative games with an infinity of players types. To this end, we introduce a sequence of nonatomic games with a finite number of players types, which approximates the initial game. We show the existence of a symmetric Wardrop equilibrium in each of these games. We prove that those symmetric equilibria converge to an equilibrium of the infinite game, and that they can be computed as solutions of finite-dimensional variational inequalities. The model is illustrated through an example from smart grids: the description of a large population of electricity consumers by a parametric distribution gives a nonatomic game with an infinity of different players types, with actions subject to coupling constraints.

article: At the heart of machine learning lies the question of generalizability of learned rules over previously unseen data. Other approaches to improving generalization include data augmentation, where the training data is artificially expanded by creating new examples from existing ones (such as rotating, flipping, and scaling images), and ensemble methods, which combine the predictions of multiple models to improve accuracy and reduce overfitting. article: We present an evaluation of several representative sampling-based and optimization-based motion planners, and then introduce an integrated motion planning system which incorporates recent advances in trajectory optimization into a sparse roadmap-based framework. This system combines the advantages of both sampling-based and optimization-based approaches to achieve high-quality, smooth, and efficient motion plans for complex robotic systems. The evaluation compares the strengths and weaknesses of different planning methods in terms of computational efficiency, scalability, solution quality, robustness, and adaptability to changing environments. The sampling-based planners, such as Rapidly-exploring Random Trees (RRTs) and Probabilistic Roadmaps (PRMs), are suitable for high-dimensional, cluttered, and dynamic environments, but tend to produce jerky and suboptimal motions. The optimization-based planners, such as Sequential Quadratic Programming (SQP) and Interior Point Methods (IPMs), can generate smooth and optimal trajectories, but are computationally expensive and sensitive to initial conditions and constraints. The integrated planning system combines the advantages of RRTs and optimization-based methods by using RRTs to search for a sparse but feasible motion roadmap in the configuration space, and then optimizing the motion with SQP or IPM to obtain a smooth and optimal trajectory that satisfies kinematic and dynamic constraints. The system incorporates a novel penalty function approach to handle constraints that are not explicitly defined by the robot's dynamics, such as obstacle avoidance, joint limits, and task constraints. The resulting motion plans are shown to be high-quality, robust, and adaptable to varying parameters and objectives. article: We would like robots to achieve purposeful manipulation by placing any instance from a category of objects into a desired set of goal states. Hence we propose a novel formulation of category-level manipulation that uses semantic 3D keypoints as the object representation. This keypoint representation enables a simple and interpretable specification of the manipulation target as geometric costs and constraints on the keypoints, which flexibly generalizes existing pose-based manipulation methods. Using this formulation, we factor the manipulation policy into instance segmentation, 3D keypoint detection, optimization-based robot action planning and local dense-geometry-based action execution. Our pipeline is robust to large intra-category shape variation and topology changes as the keypoint representation ignores task-irrelevant geometric details. The most commonly used parametric methods include Bayesian changepoint analysis, the likelihood-ratio test, and sequential hypothesis testing. In general, function refers to the purpose or activity that a structure or process serves in an organism's biology, while role refers to the place or position that an organism or structure occupies within a particular ecosystem or biological community. One approach to making this distinction is to focus on the specific mechanisms and interactions involved in a given organism or system. For example, understanding the enzymatic function of a particular protein might involve looking at its specific catalytic mechanisms, while understanding its ecological role might involve looking at its interactions with other organisms or its place within a particular food web. Another challenge in distinguishing function from role in biology is the fact that these concepts can have different meanings and implications depending on the scale or context of analysis. For example, at the molecular level, function and role might be relatively straightforward to distinguish, while at the ecosystem level, these concepts might be more complex and contingent on ecological and environmental factors. Overall, while the distinction between function and role can be difficult to apply in practice, it remains an important part of understanding the complex and interconnected workings of biological systems. article: Recent years have seen big advances in the field of sentence-level quality estimation (QE), largely as a result of using neural-based architectures. article: In recent times, using small data to train networks has become a hot topic in the field of deep learning. Reusing pre-trained parameters is one of the most important strategies to enable effective training with small data. There are various techniques available to help reuse pre-trained parameters, including transfer learning, fine-tuning and feature extraction. Transfer learning is a powerful technique that involves taking a pre-trained model that is designed for a different task, and then adapting it for a new task that we care about. For example, one could take a pre-trained image classification model, and then retrain it on a smaller dataset to perform a related task such as detecting animal species in camera traps. Fine-tuning is another technique that involves taking a pre-trained model, and then training the last few layers of the model on a new dataset. This approach is especially effective when the pre-trained model is similar to the new dataset in terms of domains and styles. Feature extraction is a technique that involves taking a pre-trained model, and then extracting the features learned by its hidden layers. These features can then be used as inputs to a new model that is trained on the new dataset. This approach is useful when we do not have enough data to directly train a new model from scratch. Overall, reusing pre-trained parameters can significantly speed up the training process, and even enable effective learning with small data.

article: A network model is considered where Poisson distributed base stations transmit to N power-domain non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) users (UEs) each that employ successive interference cancellation (SIC) for decoding. NOMA is a technique where multiple users share the same frequency and time resources, but use different power levels to transmit their signals. This allows for higher spectral efficiency. - Each NOMA user employs successive interference cancellation (SIC) for decoding. SIC is a technique where users decode the strongest signal first, remove it from the received signal, and then decode the next strongest signal. This process continues until all signals have been decoded. Overall, this network model allows for efficient use of resources and high spectral efficiency due to the use of NOMA and SIC techniques.

We propose constellation designs which are asymptotically optimal with respect to symbol error rate (SER) with an increasing number of antennas, for any finite signal to noise ratio (SNR) at the receiver, under different assumptions on the availability of CSI statistics (exact channel fading distribution or the first few moments of the channel fading distribution). We also consider the case of imperfect knowledge of the channel statistics and describe in detail the case when there is a bounded uncertainty on the moments of the fading distribution. We present numerical results on the SER performance achieved by these designs in typical scenarios and find that they may outperform existing noncoherent constellations, e.g., conventional Amplitude Shift Keying (ASK), and pilot-based schemes, e.g., Pulse Amplitude Modulation (PAM). We also observe that an optimized constellation for a specific channel distribution makes it very sensitive to uncertainties in the channel statistics. In particular, constellation designs based on optimistic channel conditions could lead to significant performance degradation in terms of the achieved symbol error rates.

article: Given a dataset V of points from some metric space, the popular k -center problem requires to identify a subset of k points (centers) in V minimizing the maximum distance of any point of V from its closest center. In this paper, we focus on two important constrained variants of the robust k -center problem, namely, the Robust Matroid Center (RMC) problem, where the set of returned centers are constrained to be an independent set of a matroid of rank k built on V, and the Robust Knapsack Center (RKC) problem, where each element I V is given a positive weight w I 1 and the aggregate weight of the returned centers must be at most 1. We devise coreset-based strategies for the two problems which yield efficient sequential, MapReduce, and Streaming algorithms. Moreover, the algorithms obliviously adapt to the intrinsic complexity of the dataset, captured by its doubling dimension D. article: Skew polynomials, which have a noncommutative multiplication rule between coefficients and an indeterminate, are the most general polynomial concept that admits the degree function with desirable properties. Then the skew polynomial ring R[x;] is defined as the set of all polynomials of the form: f (x) a0 a1x a2x2 ... anxn where ai R and x commutes with all elements of R except (r) for r R. In other words, the product of x and any element of R is not necessarily commutative unless it is the image of . The degree of a skew polynomial is defined in the same way as for commutative polynomials. The leading coefficient and highest degree term are defined in the same way as well. Skew polynomial rings have many interesting properties. For example, they are not always commutative, as the noncommutativity of R[x;] is inherited from the noncommutativity of R under the automorphism . The division algorithm is more complicated for skew polynomials, and the existence of a unique monic polynomial factorization is not guaranteed even if R is a domain. Despite these differences, skew polynomial rings still share many similarities with commutative polynomial rings. They form a graded ring, which means that we can write f (x) as a sum of homogeneous polynomials of different degrees. Skew polynomial rings also have applications in many areas of mathematics and physics. For example, they are used in the study of quantum groups, noncommutative geometry, and algebraic coding theory. In summary, skew polynomial rings are a generalization of commutative polynomial rings that have many interesting properties and applications in various fields.

article: Stock return predictability is an important research theme as it reflects our economic and social organization, and significant efforts are made to explain the dynamism therein. article: Hidden Markov chains are widely applied statistical models of stochastic processes, from fundamental physics and chemistry to finance, health, and artificial intelligence. They are used for tasks such as speech recognition, time series analysis, natural language processing, and genomic sequence analysis. In a hidden Markov model, a system's state is not observed directly, but rather through a series of observations that are probabilistically related to the underlying state. The model consists of a set of hidden states, each with an associated probability distribution over observations, and a set of transition probabilities describing how the system evolves from one state to another over time. The power of hidden Markov models lies in their ability to capture complex dependencies between observations and to model the underlying processes generating those observations. This makes them useful for tasks like speech recognition, where the observed signal is a noisy representation of the underlying spoken words. Overall, hidden Markov models are an important tool for modeling and analyzing stochastic processes in a variety of fields, and their applications are only continuing to grow as data becomes increasingly abundant and complex.

Specifically, we can measure the difference between the distribution of information in the input layer and the distribution of information in the deepest layers of the network. If this difference is beyond a certain threshold, then the input can be classified as adversarial. This method can also be used to detect the specific layer in which adversarial perturbations were introduced. article: Image forgery localization is a very active and open research field for the difficulty to handle the large variety of manipulations a malicious user can perform by means of more and more sophisticated image processing techniques. This is important for a wide range of applications, including forensics, copyright protection, and content authentication. There are various techniques employed for image forgery localization, but some of the popular ones include: 1. Copy-Move Forgery Detection: This method is used to detect and localize the region of an image in which a part has been copied and pasted, either within the same image or from another image. 2. Splicing Forgery Detection: This technique is used in cases where parts of one image have been spliced into another image. This method is used when we suspect that multiple images were used to create a single image that has been altered. 3. Retouching Forgery Detection: In this method, the focus is on detecting areas of an image that were retouched or modified using software tools like clone stamp or a healing brush. 4. Compression Artifact Analysis: Certain artifacts are created during image compression, and the analysis of these artifacts can help detect image manipulation. Overall, image forgery localization is an important field of research that is continuously advancing as image manipulation techniques continue to evolve.

article: Transient execution attacks, also called speculative execution attacks, have drawn much interest as they exploit the transient execution of instructions, e.g., during branch prediction, to leak data. Transient execution is a feature of modern processors that allows them to execute instructions speculatively ahead of time to improve performance. In a typical processor pipeline, instructions are fetched, decoded, executed, and then the results are written back to memory or a register file. However, with transient execution, instructions are fetched and executed speculatively, even before the processor has finished decoding instructions earlier in the pipeline. In the case of branch prediction, which is used to predict the outcome of a conditional jump instruction, the processor will speculatively execute the instructions in the predicted path, even if they might not be needed. This allows the processor to execute instructions faster by reducing the number of pipeline stalls caused by waiting for the outcome of a branch instruction. However, this speculative execution can potentially reveal sensitive data, particularly if the instructions being executed are accessing data that the attacker is interested in. For example, an attacker may be able to leak secrets such as encryption keys or other sensitive data by carefully crafting instructions that are executed speculatively, and then observing the effect of those instructions on the processor's cache. Transient execution attacks have been shown to be effective against modern processors, including those from Intel, AMD, and ARM. Several variants of these attacks have been identified, including Meltdown, Spectre, Foreshadow, and ZombieLoad. These attacks rely on sophisticated techniques to leak sensitive data, and mitigating them requires a combination of hardware and software changes.

article: We assume that recommender systems are more successful, when they are based on a thorough understanding of how people process information. Another strand of tagging research reveals a strong impact of time dependent forgetting on users' tag choices, such that recently used tags have a higher probability being reused than "older" tags. In this paper, we align both strands by implementing a computational theory of human memory that integrates the two-level conception and the process of forgetting in form of a tag recommender and test it in three large-scale social tagging datasets (drawn from BibSonomy, CiteULike and Flickr). As expected, our results reveal a selective effect of time: forgetting is much more pronounced on the lexical level of tags. Second, an extensive evaluation based on this observation shows that a tag recommender interconnecting both levels and integrating time dependent forgetting on the lexical level results in high accuracy predictions and outperforms other well-established algorithms, such as Collaborative Filtering, Pairwise Interaction Tensor Factorization, FolkRank and two alternative time dependent approaches. We conclude that tag recommenders can benefit from going beyond the manifest level of word co-occurrences, and from including forgetting processes on the lexical level.

article: Traffic monetization is a crucial component of running most for-profit online businesses. One of its latest incarnations is cryptocurrency mining, where a website instructs the visitor's browser to participate in building a cryptocurrency ledger in exchange for a small reward in the same currency. In its essence, this practice trades the user's electric bill, or battery level, for cryptocurrency. With user consent, this exchange can be a legitimate funding source - for example, UNICEF is collecting donations in this fashion on thehopepage.org . Regrettably, this practice also easily lends itself to abuse: in this form, called cryptojacking , attacks surreptitiously mine in the users browser, and profits are collected either by website owners or by hackers that planted the mining script into a vulnerable page. Understandably, users frown upon this practice and have sought to mitigate it by installing blacklist-based browser extensions (the top 3 for Chrome total over one million installs), whereas researchers have devised more robust methods to detect it. In turn, cryptojackers have been bettering their evasion techniques, incorporating in their toolkits domain fluxing, content obfuscation, the use of WebAssembly, and throttling. The latter, in particular, grew from being a niche feature, adopted by only one in ten sites in 2018 (,), to become commonplace in 2019, reaching an adoption ratio of 58. Whereas most state-of-the-art defenses address multiple of these evasion techniques, none is resistant against all. In this paper, we offer a novel detection method, CoinPolice, that is robust against all of the aforementioned evasion techniques. CoinPolice flips throttling against cryptojackers, artificially varying the browser's CPU power to observe the presence of throttling. Based on a deep neural network classifier, CoinPolice can detect 97.87 of hidden miners with a low false-positive rate (0.74). We compare CoinPolice performance with the current state of the art and show our approach outperforms it when detecting aggressively throttled miners. Finally, we deploy Coinpolice to perform the largest-scale cryptoming investigation to date, identifying 6700 sites that monetize traffic in this fashion.

article: In this paper we study the problem of designing a distributed graph visualization algorithm for large graphs. The algorithm must be simple to implement and the computing infrastructure must not be a limiting factor. With this in mind, we propose a decentralized approach that can efficiently handle graphs with millions or even billions of nodesedges. The algorithm works by dividing the graph into a number of partitions, each of which is assigned to a particular processor. Initially, each processor is only aware of its own partition and the connections between nodes in that partition. As the algorithm progresses, processors exchange information about their respective partitions and build a global representation of the graph. To visualize the graph, each processor independently calculates the position of nodes within its partition. We use a force-directed layout algorithm that simulates physical forces between nodes to determine their positions. The positions are then combined to create a global layout of the entire graph. To improve the efficiency of the algorithm, we use several optimization techniques. For example, we use a spatial index to reduce the number of pairwise force calculations between nodes. We also employ caching to avoid unnecessary computation when nodes remain static. Our experimental results show that our algorithm scales well with increasing graph size and number of processors. Our approach achieves a significant speedup compared to existing centralized algorithms and is able to handle extremely large graphs that would be infeasible to visualize with traditional methods.

article: In this article, we investigate the transient behavior of a sequence of packetsbits traversing a multi-hop wireless network. To study this behavior, we develop a mathematical model that captures the dynamics of packet flow through the network. We use this model to analyze various performance metrics, such as the packet delivery rate, the end-to-end delay, and the jitter (variation in delay) of packets. We also devise algorithms for controlling the flow of packets through the network, such as congestion control, routing, and scheduling. Our results show that the performance of the network depends on various factors such as the topology of the network, the traffic load, the routing algorithm used, and the size of the buffers in routers. We also find that careful tuning of these factors can result in significant improvements in the performance of the network, such as higher packet delivery rates and lower end-to-end delays. article: Although artificial neural networks have shown great promise in applications including computer vision and speech recognition, there remains considerable practical and theoretical difficulty in optimizing their parameters. Additionally, optimizing these parameters can take a significant amount of time and computational resources. One approach to address the optimization challenges of neural networks is to use automated techniques, such as grid search or random search, to explore the parameter space and find the best settings. Another common approach is to use gradient descent, which updates the parameters iteratively based on the gradients of the loss function with respect to the parameters. However, gradient descent can get stuck in local minima and suffer from issues like vanishing gradients and exploding gradients. To address some of the optimization challenges, several advanced optimization techniques have been proposed, such as momentum-based methods, adaptive learning rate methods, and second-order methods. article: It is well established that neural networks with deep architectures perform better than shallow networks for many tasks in machine learning. We benchmark the models, focussing on the accuracy of generating energetic observables near the phase transition, where these quantities are most difficult to approximate. Interestingly, after training the generative networks, we observe that the accuracy essentially depends only on the number of neurons in the first hidden layer of the network, and not on other model details such as network depth or model type. article: Unlike nonconvex optimization, where gradient descent is guaranteed to converge to a local optimizer, algorithms for nonconvex-nonconcave minimax optimization can have topologically different solution paths: sometimes converging to a solution, sometimes oscillating, and sometimes not converging at all. To tackle such problems, researchers have proposed a variety of optimization techniques, such as stochastic gradient descent, evolutionary algorithms, game theory-based approaches, and other heuristic methods. These methods often require a delicate balance between exploration and exploitation, and can be quite sensitive to the problem parameters and initial conditions. In summary, nonconvex-nonconcave minimax optimization is a challenging problem that requires careful consideration of both the problem structure and the optimization algorithm used to solve it. As a helpful assistant, I suggest consulting with experts in the field and conducting thorough experimentation to determine the best approach for a given problem.

article: We prove a quantum information-theoretic conjecture due to Ji, Liu and Song (CRYPTO 2018) which suggested that a uniform superposition with random binary phase is statistically indistinguishable from a Haar -random state with high probability. The conjecture can be stated formally as follows: Let psi be a uniform superposition of n qubits with random binary phases such that: psi 1sqrt (2n) (0 e (itheta1) 1) (0 e (itheta2) 1) ... (0 e (ithetan) 1) where each thetai is chosen uniformly at random from {0,pi}. Overall, the result has important implications for quantum cryptography and quantum algorithms, as it provides a new way of generating highly entangled states that are statistically indistinguishable from random states, but can be generated efficiently using quantum circuits.

[SODA'07] and Koutsoupias and Vidali [MFCS'07], respectively. More specifically, we show that the currently best lower bound of 2.618 can be achieved even for just n 4 machines; for n 5 we already get the first improvement, namely 2.711; and allowing the number of machines to grow arbitrarily large we can get a lower bound of 2.755 .

article: Although blockchain, the supporting technology of Bitcoin and various cryptocurrencies, has offered a potentially effective framework for numerous applications, it still suffers from the adverse affects of the impossibility triangle. The recent introduction of error correcting codes in sharded blockchain by Li et al. partially settles this trilemma, boosting throughput without compromising security and decentralization. In this paper, we improve the coded sharding scheme in three ways. First, we propose a novel 2-Dimensional Sharding strategy, which inherently supports cross-shard transactions, alleviating the need for complicated inter-shard communication protocols. Second, we employ distributed storage techniques in the propagation of blocks, improving latency under restricted bandwidth. Finally, we incorporate polynomial cryptographic primitives of low degree, which brings coded blockchain techniques into the realm of feasible real-world parameters.

article: Orthogonal greedy learning (OGL) is a stepwise learning scheme that starts with selecting a new atom from a specified dictionary via the steepest gradient descent (SGD) and then builds the estimator through orthogonal projection. Based on the new greedy criterion, we derive an adaptive termination rule for OGL. Our theoretical study shows that the new learning scheme can achieve the existing (almost) optimal learning rate of OGL. Plenty of numerical experiments are provided to support that the new scheme can achieve almost optimal generalization performance, while requiring less computation than OGL.

article: In this paper, we develop a Bayesian evidence maximization framework to solve the sparse non-negative least squares problem (S-NNLS). We also propose a novel Bayesian evidence maximization algorithm based on variational inference to estimate the optimal hyperparameters of the RGSM prior. Our framework also incorporates a sparsity inducing prior on the estimated coefficients to ensure that the solution remains sparse. We can use a Cantonese speech dataset like HKUST as our target data. During fine-tuning, the model's weights are updated to better match the Cantonese acoustic characteristics. We can also perform data augmentation techniques such as speed perturbation and adding background noise to increase the robustness of the model. Once the fine-tuning is complete, we can evaluate the model on a separate test set to measure its speech recognition accuracy. We can also compare the model's performance to other Cantonese ASR systems. In summary, transfer learning of a Mandarin ASR model to Cantonese can be a useful approach for developing a basic ASR system for low-resource languages. It can save time and resources while still achieving high accuracy.

The quasi-conformal map in the plane facilitates the Calderon-based approach for anisotropic conductivities. The method is demonstrated on discontinuous radially symmetric conductivities of high and low contrast. Keywords . Calderon's problem, anisotropic, electrical impedance tomography, quasi-conformal map, exponential solutions, inverse conductivity problem, Dirichlet-to-Neumann map

article: A dynamical neural network consists of a set of interconnected neurons that interact over time continuously. It can exhibit computational properties in the sense that the dynamical system's evolution andor limit points in the associated state space can correspond to numerical solutions to certain mathematical optimization or learning problems. Such a computational system is particularly attractive in that it can be mapped to a massively parallel computer architecture for power and throughput efficiency, especially if each neuron can rely solely on local information (i.e., local memory). Deriving gradients from the dynamical network's various states while conforming to this last constraint, however, is challenging. We show that by combining ideas of top-down feedback and contrastive learning, a dynamical network for solving the l 1 -minimizing dictionary learning problem can be constructed, and the true gradients for learning are provably computable by individual neurons. Using spiking neurons to construct our dynamical network, we present a learning process, its rigorous mathematical analysis, and numerical results on several dictionary learning problems.

article: We consider convolutional networks from a reproducing kernel Hilbert space viewpoint. The decompositions can be viewed as generalizations of the Fourier series for periodic functions or the Taylor series for smooth functions. In this case, the elementary functions are called "convolutional harmonics," which are a family of functions representing the different frequencies of the convolution operation. The use of convolutional harmonics allows us to better understand and interpret the behavior of convolutional networks, and also provides a framework for designing more efficient and effective network architectures. Additionally, the theory of reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces provides a rigorous mathematical foundation for studying convolutional networks and their properties.

article: lettrine Lesion segmentation from the surrounding skin is the first task for developing automatic Computer-Aided Diagnosis of skin cancer. Variant features of lesion like uneven distribution of color, irregular shape, and varying texture make the segmentation task challenging. There are various methods developed for lesion segmentation such as thresholding, region-growing, edge detection, and machine learning-based approaches. Thresholding is a simple and easy-to-use technique where a threshold value is selected to separate the lesion from the surrounding skin. However, thresholding might not work well for lesions with complex textures or color variations. Region-growing is a technique that starts from a seed point inside the lesion and grows the region by adding adjacent pixels that have similar properties. This method can segment complex irregular shapes, but the selection of seed point can be crucial. Edge detection techniques segment lesions by detecting the boundaries between lesion and skin. However, this method may fail to segment textured or homogeneously colored lesions. Machine learning-based segmentation techniques use algorithms to learn from given training data and make predictions on new data. These techniques have shown promising results in lesion segmentation but require a significant amount of training data. Overall, lesion segmentation is a challenging task requiring expertise and specialized techniques.

article: We look into the connection between the musical and lyrical content of metal music by combining automated extraction of high-level audio features and quantitative text analysis on a corpus of 124.288 song lyrics from this genre. For a subsample of 503 songs, scores for predicting perceived musical hardnessheaviness and darknessgloominess were extracted using audio feature models. By combining both audio feature and text analysis, we (1) offer a comprehensive overview of the lyrical topics present within the metal genre and (2) are able to establish whether or not levels of hardness and other music dimensions are associated with the occurrence of particularly harsh (and other) textual topics. Twenty typical topics were identified and projected into a topic space using multidimensional scaling (MDS). After Bonferroni correction, positive correlations were found between musical hardness and darkness and textual topics dealing with ' brutal death ', ' dystopia ', ' archaisms and occultism ', ' religion and satanism ', ' battle ' and ' (psychological) madness ', while there is a negative associations with topics like ' personal life ' and ' love and romance '.

article: Voice activity detection (VAD), used as the front end of speech enhancement, speech and speaker recognition algorithms, determines the overall accuracy and efficiency of the algorithms. To overcome this problem, a novel ensemble-based approach using SVM has been proposed in this paper. The performance of the proposed ensemble structure has been compared with a The performance of the proposed ensemble structure has been compared with a feedforward neural network (NN). Although NN performs better than single SVM-based VAD trained on a small portion of the training data, ensemble SVM gives accuracy comparable to neural network-based VAD. Ensemble SVM and NN give 88.74 and 86.28 accuracy respectively whereas the stand-alone SVM shows 57.05 accuracy on average on the test dataset.

article: How far and how fast does information spread in social media? Researchers have recently examined a number of factors that affect information diffusion in online social networks, including: the novelty and perceived importance of the information, the credibility of its source, the level of engagement and participation of users, and the structure and size of the network. In general, information can spread quickly and to a large audience in social media, particularly if it is novel, attention-grabbing, and emotionally charged. The speed and reach of diffusion can be influenced by various factors, such as the level of interconnectedness among users, the frequency of sharing and exposure, the use of hashtags and other viral mechanisms, and the timing of posts. Additionally, the type of platform and its algorithms for content distribution can also play a role in shaping information diffusion patterns. Ultimately, the effectiveness of information diffusion in social media depends on a complex interplay of social, psychological, and technological factors.

article: Ethereum has emerged as the most popular smart contract development platform, with hundreds of thousands of contracts stored on the blockchain and covering a variety of application scenarios, such as auctions, trading platforms, and so on. Given their financial nature, security vulnerabilities may lead to catastrophic consequences and, even worse, they can be hardly fixed as data stored on the blockchain, including the smart contract code itself, are immutable. An automated security analysis of these contracts is thus of utmost interest, but at the same time technically challenging for a variety of reasons, such as the specific transaction-oriented programming mechanisms, which feature a subtle semantics, and the fact that the blockchain data which the contract under analysis interacts with, including the code of callers and callees, are not statically known. In this work, we present eThor , the first sound and automated static analyzer for EVM bytecode, which is based on an abstraction of the EVM bytecode semantics based on Horn clauses. In particular, our static analysis supports reachability properties, which we show to be sufficient for capturing interesting security properties for smart contracts (e.g., single-entrancy) as well as contract-specific functional properties. Our analysis is proven sound against a complete semantics of EVM bytecode and an experimental large-scale evaluation on real-world contracts demonstrates that eThor is practical and outperforms the state-of-the-art static analyzers: specifically, eThor is the only one to provide soundness guarantees, terminates on 95 of a representative set of real-world contracts, and achieves an F -measure (which combines sensitivity and specificity) of 89.

article: Accurate rainfall forecasting is critical because it has a great impact on people's social and economic activities. Furthermore, deep learning algorithms have been shown to outperform traditional statistical techniques in forecasting accuracy. This is because deep learning algorithms are able to handle large and complex datasets, as well as detect subtle relationships between input and output variables. Overall, deep learning models have the potential to revolutionize rainfall forecasting and provide more accurate and reliable predictions. However, it is important to note that environmental factors such as climate change can also impact rainfall patterns, and these should be taken into account when developing forecasting models. Additionally, continuous monitoring and updating of these models will be necessary to ensure their accuracy and effectiveness over time.

article: We initiate the study of indivisible chore allocation for agents with asymmetric shares. The fairness concept we focus on is the weighted natural generalization of maxmin share: WMMS fairness and we aim to design a mechanism that achieves such fairness. More specifically, we consider a setting where agents have heterogeneous values for the same chore, and we want to allocate the chore in a way that maximizes the minimum weighted payoff for each agent. This involves assigning different weights to each agent's valuation of the chore and taking the minimum of the weighted payoffs. One approach to achieve WMMS fairness in chore allocation is to use market-based mechanisms. In these mechanisms, agents bid on the chore and the chore is allocated to the bidder with the highest bid. However, to achieve WMMS fairness, we need to modify the usual bidding mechanism to take into account the weights assigned to each agent's valuation. One way to do this is to use a weighted Vickrey-Clarke-Groves (VCG) mechanism, where the payment each agent is charged is proportional to the change in the minimum weighted payoff caused by their presence in the allocation. Another approach is to use algorithmic mechanisms, such as the random priority rule, to generate a random allocation of the chore that is proportional to the weights assigned to each agent's valuation. In this case, we can prove that the expected minimum weighted payoff is equal to a certain fraction of the maximum possible minimum weighted payoff, which provides a guarantee of WMMS fairness. Overall, there are different mechanisms that can be used to achieve WMMS fairness in chore allocation for agents with asymmetric shares, and the choice of mechanism depends on the specific application and constraints of the problem.
