article: Catherine sat at her desk, looking out the bedroom window above it at the vast expanse of brown fields and dying grass far below her. A light snow had begun to fall over the sullen landscape, dotting the dark fields with bright spots of white. Any ordinary girl would have been crying, but crying was not Catherine's nature. She sat looking out over the countryside, as stiff and frozen as the glaciers beyond the plains on the horizon. It's useless. I'll never get my powers to awaken. Kristina was only fourteen when she first awakened hers. I'm twenty years of age now, with nothing to show for it. Soon, even my lineage will come into question. Without warning, Rickford burst into the room. "Catherine, you have to come quickly!" He was gasping for breath, and his eyes were wide with panic. "It's them, the foreigners. They're here for your family!" Catherine spun around in her chair, knocking it to the ground in violence. "What." Her gaze was piercing as she stared down the young, pale guard standing at the entrance to her room. "And the guards? Surely our defenses are strong enough to stop them?" "Either dead or fleeing for their lives," Rickford panted. "The palace has been overrun." "Impossible." Catherine walked over to the entrance. "It would take an army to take down the palace. I've been looking out across the field for the last hour. Nobody has been coming." Rickford leaned in close to whisper into Catherine's ear. "Commander Watson is saying he thinks it was an inside job. A guard mutiny." Catherine's face boiled over with anger. "It was Drake's unit. He's been plotting my demise for years. That foreigner had no business standing guard in my castle. I'll have his head for this." Rickford nodded solemnly. "We can deal with him later. Right now your safety is my top priority." The two figures fled down the spiral staircase to the landing below. Catherine's breath was coming in short gasps. How could this happen? Is my family allright? Kristina lives on the top floor, did she make it out okay? The duo fled down a narrow side hall and approached a small wooden door. Rickford turned to Catherine, his face suddenly filled with sorrow. "Catherine, before we go any further, I just want you to know that I've always loved you. It pains me that I could never be with you, and I'm sorry about all this." Catherine looked at him, confused by the timing of his confession. "Rickford, Now it not the time for this! None of this is your fault! We're making this out alive and we can discuss this later." "No, it is the time," Rickford continued. "I always loved you, but your sister..... she..... she's awful." His expression darkened. "That witch will destroy this country. Sometimes, you must but bury passions in the name of the country you serve." Before Catherine could respond, Rickford pushed open the door. Inside was a room, dimly lit by a pair of torches hung from the wall. Through the darkness, she could make out four to five figures, shrouded in shadow. "Who is it?" Commander Watson's gravelly voice barked. "It's me," Rickford answered. "And I've brought her." Catherine turned to Rickford, bewildered. "What's going on here Rickford?" Rickford didn't answer, but grabbed her arm forcefully. Catherine felt her stomach drop. "I'm sorry," he said replied again. "For the country." "Good work son," Watson answered. "Shoot her, and quickly. Then go fetch the queen and do the same." "Yes sir," Rickford answered, tears welling up in his eyes. His gun was already out, and trained on Catherine. "WAIT," Catherine screamed. "Rickford please! If you love me, then stop this madness!" Rickford said nothing. The barrel of his gun trembled as he leveled it with Catherine's head. This all felt like a nightmare. She had known Rickford since he was a child, how could he do this? None of that mattered now. There was nothing she could do, except shut her eyes tightly, and wait for the inevitable. As she did so, she started to feel something warm well up from the inside of her stomach. Fire, she realized. At once, she felt a faint glimmer of excitement. So this is what it feels like to become awakened. She opened her eyes. Rickford, still trembling, gasped. Her eyes were bright and glowing like embers. "No, I'm sorry Rickford. Sorry, for you." Watson realized what was about to happen, a second too late. "SHE HAS THE GIFT TOO. SHOOT HER N He was cut off as an orange blast rocked the room, blossoming from Catherine's chest like a flower in spring. Rickford and the other guards were thrown backward by a fiery shockwave, and lay crumpled in pile in the corner of the small room. Catherine sprang up from the ground and threw open the door, running back out the way that she came. Another guard was were waiting for her at the entrance. "Where do you think your going?" he asked, as he raised his gun to face her. "I knew Rickford didn't have the guts to finish you off, that useless pimply faced greenhorn." He spat on the ground at his name. "Not a problem for me. I've been waiting a long time for this." Frantically, Catherine tried to channel more fire, but to no avail. The first blast of fire had drained her completely. This is the end, she thought. A shot rang out across the corridor. Catherine looked down at herself, expecting to see blood. Miraculously, she was fine. She turned back to the guard, as he fell to the floor, lifeless. Drake the Foreigner was standing behind him, the barrel of his firearm still smoking. He holstered his rifle as Catherine looked back at him in shock. "Princess, upper command of the Palace Guard has been compromised. They have conspired to kill you and your family. It is now my sole duty to ensure your protection. Please follow me if you value your life." Edit: Thanks everyone for reading! article: EDIT: THIS IS CURRENTLY A LIVE DOCUMENT. REFRESH EVERY FEW MINUTES TO GET MORE STORY. I breathed a sigh of relief as I plopped down on my sofa. Mr.Fibbles jumped up and rubbed his head against my leg. " Hey, buddy. " I sighed. " I think I got the job. " A slow smile crept across my face as I contently vegetated on my couch. The last couple of days had been a flurry of studying up on the most recent cryptography breakthroughs in science. Being an unemployed computer science major was a rarity these days, but I had been going through a lot. A year ago I sure as hell wasn't sober, and Eva had just broken up with me. But now, my life was back on track. The NSA had seemed pleased as I walked out the door, although I felt the vague feeling they were watching me to the car. " Things are finally looking up, Fibbles. " I purred. I turned on Netflix, but soon I was asleep, dreaming- finally- of having peace. " Are you sure he's the best one? " The voice was gruff. Unforgiving. Scarred. " He's the only one. Darned instagram and snapchat make it suspicious if someone disappears for a few days, let alone their whole lives. " " What makes him different, then, dammit? " The voice came into focus. It was wearing a uniform. It had been tempered by steel. " For one, he quit all social media when he became a different person, a year ago, after he decided to sober u- " " That's just the thing! The last thing we need is this... this... guy drinking all the ethanol in sick bay when we need him on the computer! " " All reconnaissance done in the last 6 months seems to indicate he's completely clean- a changed man, even. Just him and his cat. " The General growled again, but said nothing. " Sir, you said it yourself a few days ago... if we can't find someone soon, the situation on Domus goes from what we have... to complete anarchy. All the last 50 years, gone. " The General seemed to be contemplating, grinding his jaw and glaring at the screen. Finally, he nodded. " Send them in. " I woke up with a start. Had I imagined the knocking? The downstairs couple always seemed to be knocking chairs over. Maybe that was it... I layed down and closed my eyes... The noise again. Groaning, I threw the sheets off my face and looked at my alarm. 2:30 am. Dead of night, the burning neon told me. Who was it? A pit of ice settled in my stomach. Was it Alex, back for his money from 2 years ago? Was it Frank, needing another quick fix? Dreamlike, I drifted to the door, afraid to look out. The ice cube melted as I saw a pair of suited men. Tax collectors I could deal with. As I unbolted the door and creaked it open, fearful I'd wake Mrs.Whitcomb up down the hall, I groggily began to wonder if this had to do with the interview. Too late. " Mr.Tim Lodz? " The men asked. I nodded after a few moments. Behind me, I felt Mr.Fibbles slide in between my legs. I gently kicked him back. " Tim Lodz, the programmer? " I nodded again. What a strange question at 2:30. " Tim Lodz, parents deceased, no family at all? " The men were huge, dressed in black business suits. If I saw them walking down the street- if I noticed them at all- I'd hardly think they were anything but normal. " I hardly think I should be answering a question like that at... at... " " 2:32 in the morning. " One of them answered without a beat. " May we come in? " The other said, cracking his neck. " I hardly think that this is the time for... social calls. " My brain was still groggy. They didn't listen, and pushed into my apartment. " Hey there! " My voice was rising. I was fully awake now. " Who do you think you are, barging in here like that!" They both looked at me. "Sir, close the door." Neck crack said that. "The sooner we talk, the sooner we can leave." "We leave? I think you've got something wrong, buddy! This is my house, and you'll be leaving!" They looked at each other, and without a word marched over to me and picked me up, each holding an arm. They dragged me over to my lazy boy, and threw me in. Mr Fibbles watched safely. "Coward." I whispered. They both sat down on the sofa- the same spot Sally died. I pushed that thought out of my memory. I sat up attentively. If I was being robbed, they were holding themselves quite well. In my sleep addled mind, I gave a slight giggle. Were they here to tell me I was special? A wizard? Maybe. The thought made me smile. If neck crack could have rolled his eyes, he would have. "My name is agent Smith. And my friend here is agent Ferrier." "Creative names." I quipped. I was feeling bold. They looked at each other again. The one called Ferrier began to speak, iron jaw locked in position. "Mr.Lodz. As you know, you were recently interviewed for a computer programmer position at the NSA." I was right! They were here about the job. "The interview went far better than expected, and you have been accepted." "Great!" I yelled. "But did you guys have to wake me up to tell me that?" I paused a bit. "Accepted to what?" Smith stood up. "Sir, what we are about to tell you might shock you. But you must listen. Your immediate future is at stake. The U.S. government, alongside Russia, China, India, and the European Union, have created stations on a number of worlds, including bases on the moon, mars, and Europa." My jaw hung open. Where were the cameras? Was this some kind of TV show? Mr.Smith cleared his throat. "13 years ago, the U.S. government discovered the secrets to faster than light travel. I'm not a scientist, but try to think of it like'tearing a hole in the space time' to shrink distance." I nodded, but a slight grin overtook my face. They had to be joking. "I assure you, this is not a joke, Mr.Lodz. The aforementioned powers colonized Proxima Centauri b, at first only a few buildings, but now home to about 600 researchers. Recentlly, the station has come under internal threat from a number of dissidents, who are targeting the station's transceivers and storage bank "Hold up..." I chuckled. "If this Faster-Than-Light thing really was real, why not just tell everyone? What's the harm?" "The drive has..... other capabilities. If detonated inside an atmosphere, it instantly becomes equivalent to 100 atomic bombs, vaporizing whole states." I held up my finger. "Well, if there really are terrorists on your compound, you guys still screwed up then! Check your potholes. This screenplay still has a few of them." A vein bulged on Ferriers neck. "The dissidents are not your typical terrorist. In fact, they are all researchers. The matter currently in dispute is the level of autonomy that this colony currently has." "You guys are fighting people who want you to take more direct control?" Now Smith looked annoyed. "Mr.Lodz, it is the U.S. government's policy to exert control over a research station on this planet as we would any other." I snorted. Ferrier looked at his watch. "We're running out of time." Smith glared beneath his glasses. "Mr.Lodz, would you like to join this group of individuals on the planet?" I threw my hands up, and stood out of my chair. "Hell yeah! But I don't know what the hell you guys have been smok Ferrier was behind me. I hadn't even heard him move. I felt a cold needle plunge into my neck, and fell a great distance..... Behind me, I heard Fibbles meow. Good boy. Was my last thought.

article: The reason is water pressure. Pressure wants to equalize. So when you are running 1 tap, you are getting all the pressure, and when someone turns on another tap you are sharing the pressure with that tap, which reduces the pressure you were initially getting. This is because the water flow is being split between the two taps, and each tap is now receiving less water pressure than before. The more taps that are opened, the more the pressure is shared between them, resulting in lower pressure at each tap. This is why it's important to properly size your plumbing system and choose the right fixtures to ensure proper water pressure throughout your home.

article: Part I: A week ago, Galaxy 8's Interstellar Detective Bureau dispatched an investigator to mining vessel Tau-9-9 to inquire into details involving the mass murder and data breach on Watcher station Alpha-0-1-1. Security footage was sparse, but it revealed a human astronaut absconding from the station with a small data stick. Security footage at port 119B revealed a security seal from astronauts on Tau-9-9 was used to gain access to the station shortly before the massacre. This station was manned by only two officers. One, a top-decorated pilot in the U.S. Air Force and mother of two named Amanda Bailey. The other, a Harvard-educated mathematician from Japan who played video games as a hobby and spoke 19 different languages named Ken Ichimitzu. The investigator's entrance into the mining ship was unnoticed and silent. The ship appeared unoccupied. It looked ransacked, though. Furniture was torn and clawed through, almost as if by an animal. A small veneer of dust had settled over all, and motion-detecting lights creaked on as he walked down hallways, almost as if they'd been dormant for some time. With the mainframe hard-drive missing, the investigator made his way down several corridors to the captain's quarters. There, he ignited the computer, unfurled a small piece of crinkled paper containing a username and passcode, and accessed the Captain's log file. Captain's Log: 82616 3:30 a.m. Eyes hurt from digging knuckles of my hands into my eyes, trying to wipe away the sleep. I feel trapped. Helpless. Out here on this space station, my computer monitor is really the only area of activity, of newness, of anything echoing life back home. Looks like that buffoon Trump is going to lose. Not much better to beat him, but hey, whoever gets me back home safe and sound, right? I should be catching sheep by now, but something's keeping me awake. I don't feel right about Amanda. My toes won't rest in their shoes, my shoulders feel tight, I'm breathing shallowly, and there's a nameless thickness set into his throat that won't go away. I swear I've looked at the clock ten times in the last minute. It's 3:16 now. Damn it. It had started last week. Astronaut 11A (aka Amanda), had returned on Saturday from her monthly meeting on exoplanet Rebinium with the other watchers on star system Tau-9-9. I had asked her how the meeting went, and curiously she didn't talk much about it. She loves these things, the ideas they have for new exploration and resource management, and all the new people she meets there. But this time she just yawned, and then asked where the bathroom was. It's a small spacecraft. And she's been here for almost a year now. I glanced at her in incredulity, you know, the way you do when you are trying to persuade someone into stopping joking around, to see if they're serious, with that hint of hope and terror that what if she really doesn't know..... my eye brows raised and forehead scrunched in confusion. She immediately sensed my nerves and the gaffe, and laughed, but it was a laugh that was hollow and perfunctory, a laugh like when you are trying to disarm someone, not when you find something funny. Certainly not the kind of giddy laugh I've grown to love about Amanda. But when she turned around to walk away, she took a right turn instead of a left one, and even though I'd turned around out of politeness, so as to hide the fact I was worried, I could hear soft footsteps trying to conceal their way behind my back, retracing steps back to the bathroom. Maybe I'm paranoid. Maybe she just took some strange medicine or something, and was a little delirious. Hence, the fatigue. Who knows. Over and out. Captain's Log: 82716 12:21 a.m. "I don't feel right," were her first words when I saw her the following morning. I asked if she didn't sleep well, and she said it wasn't that. Something in her head, she said, striking her skull sort of violently with the heel of her hand. But she wouldn't talk anymore about it the more I asked. It's not like her. She's one of the most open people I know, a great American in that true Karl Popper sense. I'm worried about her. The work on the ship is going smoothly. She's still crunching out her reports on status of the ununpentium-289 mining operation. This element is extremely friable, with a half life of one-fifth of a second, about as long as it takes you to sneeze. But a couple of important articles are missing, and I can't seem to turn them up anywhere. One of the astronaut suits is gone, and the picture of my wife and kids I keep paper-clipped to my bathroom mirror has disappeared. I can't figure out which is more important. Captain's Log: 82816 Amanda has a massive bruise on the right side of her head. I asked her if she was hitting herself, and she replied in a cloying voice that she was perfectly fine and happy to be awake and at work. I found it dodgy, but I was glad she was okay. Ever since that trip through the teleporter, she's been acting weird. She doesn't eat eggs anymore for breakfast. That was her favorite food. Now it's granola. I also ran a bot program to monitor her computer activities during breakout session from the helm. She's been ignoring attempts by her family to Skype with her lately, which is quite unlike her. When she was in the shower, I snuck into her room to peek around a bit, see if everything was all right. What's unusual is that her own picture of her family, framed on her bureau, it's gone, too. And I still can't find that damned astronaut suit. Captain's Log: 82916 Today we had food delivery. It went well, partly because I did all the work, but partly because Amanda was not around for me to stress about. It was nice just to be by myself, even if the docking, receiving, depressurization, importing, documentation, transportation, and storage and sealing of the materials was a lot of work. It was worth it, to be alone. I never thought I'd want to be alone, that I'd ever write that, out here on this spaceship. But I like it. When Amanda didn't show up for lunch, I knew something was off. Regardless of my personal preference not to see if she was okay, I took a brisk stroll down to dormitories and rapped on her door. After brushing me off with a few grunts, she opened the door. She was naked, dripping with water. Her eyes, they were hungry. She pulled me into her room, threw her thighs around me, and we had sex then and there. She has a husband for God's sake. I felt strange about it, still do. She didn't seem to care about any of it. And when I finished, she rolled away and said she had some work to do on the computer. She didn't even wipe it out, it was trickling out of her onto the chair she was sitting in, beading down like saliva onto the rubber floor. Who is this person? Captain's Log: 83016 There is something disturbing about Amanda. Lest you begin to think this log is becoming a softcore porno, let me officially document that I wanted and didn't want to see her again. Against my better judgment, I scheduled a trace program to generate data about her internet traffic, what she was reading and writing, and in general why she wasn't working from her office desk in the star bay. Shortly after initiating the program, one of the sensors in the docking bay went dark. Putting down the report I was finishing on the station's Silent Running greenhouse garden, I threw on a track suit and jogged across the station to examine the cause for its failure. As I was inspecting the sensor, I sensed someone right behind me, the hairs on the back of my neck stood up. I turned halfway, and out of the corner of my eye a massive figure towered over me. Immediately I threw my back against the wall and cowered, gasping, seconds later realizing it was just Amanda. I yelled at her for sneaking up on me. Her hair was all tangled, knotty, and there was a musky smell pouring out around her, a smell that wasn't attractive. She asked my why I was spying on her. This was when I felt nauseated. She didn't ask it in the sense that she was innocent. It was malicious. There was something malevolent in her voice I had never heard before. But her face was cool, hands flat at her sides, voice monotone, but there was an indistinct contempt running in the background. I bought some time and told her that Tau-9-9 protocol requires documentation of company time during periods of employment, and that I was simply trying to account for her employment hours so that she could get paid - not that I was reading what she was up to. She asked if I had seen the report. I told her I hadn't, which was true. The report was scheduled to finish two hours ago, and I'd just been involved with other things. Immediately she relaxed, and half-smiled. Then she reached past me into the sensor, pulled a wire and linked it to a node, and the room lit up like a police roof light. Before she left, I asked her if she had seen my family photo. There was a kind of dim shaking in her irises. Like something deep in her was stirring from slumber. Then she shook her head, smacked it again hard, turned around and walked out. Just before she left, she said families make one weak, and are inappropriate for this profession. Then the airlock door hissed, and she was gone. Captain's Log: 9116 The report is gone! I logged into my account, plugged into Tau-9-9's mainframe, and tried to access the data file, but it was corrupted. Something in the code had warped, and it was unusable. Things just get weirder and weirder around here. Today Amanda was walking on her hands up and down the star bay, almost singing.

I'm well aware that my sampling of feminist thought is probably not representative of most feminists. With that said: I have often heard it said that the major factors in the incidence of rape are something along these lines: The media portrays women as sexualized objects, thus discouraging boys and young men from seeing women as fully human. This leads men to think that it is okay for them to rape women. We do not teach our males what consent is. Alternatively, we don't teach them that it is not okay to rape women. Now, I don't think that the first reason is a totally invalid point. I agree that the media sexualizes women to an obscene degree, and I'm sure that that has deleterious effects on the psyche of both males an females. The second point seems totally absurd to me, though. I believe that rapists know that what they're doing is wrong, but they choose to do it anyway. This goes for all kinds of rape, too. I think that both the violent rapist and the frat guy who pressures a girl into getting wasted at a party and then has sex with her while she's semi-unconscious know that what they're doing is wrong. Rather than these two points, I think that the main contributing factors to rape are psychological issues that occur as a result of trauma in childhood. I don't have any statistics to back this up, so please lambast me if this is wrong: I believe that the majority of rape victims were the victim of some sort of major abuse in childhood, most likely sexual. I also believe that the same goes for the perpetrators of abuse. People who were abused in childhood almost always reflect the repercussions of their abuse in their demeanor, and abusers can sense that. I'm not talking about anything magical, either. In my experience, victims of abuse carry themselves differently and can have personality traits that indicate that they were abused. Abusers recognize that and seek those people out as victims. In summary, I think that the main contributing factor in the incidence of rape is childhood abuse of both future victim and perpetrator. I believe that dehumanization of women through sexualization in media is a much smaller factor, and that media influence alone cannot take a boy who grew up in a healthy and supportive family and turn him into a rapist. I think that if media does have any significant effect in the incidence of rape, it is only because it reinforces the already sick foundation of someone who was abused.

The most important thing to consider is simply how much money is the toy store making. If the toy store is making 100 every day, that means it is making roughly 3,000 (30 days of 100) every month, or 36,000 every year (12 months of 3,000). Let's suppose we are able to figure that the toy store should be able to keep making this much for the next ten years. Then we could consider that the entire toy store is worth 360,000 (which is 36,000 for ten years). Now, in practice this is a lot more complicated. But the basic principle is simply to figure out how much money a company can be expected to make in a certain time frame. Fortunately, we don't have to figure it out ourselves. There are big companies whose job is to figure out how much other companies are worth, and they do all of the hard work for us. If we want to buy it (and if he is willing to sell it), we can pay Mr. Jones that much money and now the toy store is ours! Now, this is all well and good if we have 360,000 and we want to own the entire company. But let's suppose we only have half that much, we have 180,000. What can we do now? Well, as long as Mr. Jones is willing, we can buy half of his company instead of the whole thing. This means that we will own 50 or half of the company, and he will own the other half. That means that instead of all of the money from selling toys going to Mr. Jones, half will go to him and the other half to us. Another way of saying that we own 50 of the company is to say that we own 50 of the stock in a company. When a company is set up in a way that you can buy pieces of it, those pieces are called stock. There are two ways to think about stock: percentages, and shares. What we just talked about are percentages. We can buy 50 of the shares in Mr. Jones' toy company for 180,000. Similarly, we could buy 10 of the shares in Mr. Jones' toy company for 36,000 (assuming the total value of the company was 360,000), or we could buy 1 of the shares for 3,600, and so on. When you hear people talk about stocks, you will hear them talk about shares of stock. What exactly does this mean? article: To domesticate a species is to change it in some radical ways through many generations of breeding. That is what we did with dogs, cats, cows, pig, chickens, etc. The domesticated animals bear little resemblance to the original species they were selected from. In Russia and experiment was done to see if they could domesticate foxes. From a large initial population, they carefully selected the least aggressive, most human tolerant individuals for breeding and discarded the rest. After many generations of such selection they had friendly, cuddly foxes. But they didn't look like foxes anymore; most had short curly tails, shorter snouts, and were multicoloured. So you can't just bring a wild animal like a racoon into the house and make it into a pet (though it may sometimes work on an individual basis). A group of scientists tried this with wolves. They had to discontinue the experiment because it was too dangerous. No matter how much love and affection and training they would give the cubs, as soon as they reached sexual maturity they became aggressive to the humans and seemed to forget completely all the love and kindness.," "It's really just a matter of not having tried. We have domesticated deer actually, on hunting ranges. And foxes in Russia. But, like uYMK1234 said, why the heck would you want to domesticate a raccoon? There is no point, so we don't try to do it.

article: Well before we had the planets, we had a disc of dust orbiting the sun. This is because when the initial cloud (which formed the sun) collapsed due to gravity , it began to spin, flattening into a disc shape due to centrifugal force. As the disc cooled, tiny particles of dust and gas came together, forming larger and larger clumps through a process called accretion. These clumps eventually became planetesimals, which then collided and merged to form the planets we know today. It's incredible to think about how our solar system and its planets came into existence through this process!

article: "And since when has swearing in public been an imprisonable offence?" I asked. The officer didn't even break stride as he put my arms behind my back. The cafe owner, one of the few left trading honestly, looked terrified. He hadn't meant to provoke me to the point of swearing. Once I had said'for fuck's sake' the police had been called in, and as is usual in this day and age they come pretty quick - after all, there were very few people left to arrest. I resisted. "Resisting isn't going to get you anywhere," the police officer said. "You are under arrest I looked at the shopkeeper. Did he dare? The cop had his handcuffs out. I kicked out, my heel striking the cop's shinbone, and as he reeled backwards I turned around to face him. He looked surprised, but there was something more - terror. US cops were not used to resistance anymore. Seeing this, I threw everything into my punch. The crunch of the cop's nose breaking was followed with the thud as his back hit a table. I stuck out my foot, and the cop went over it, crashed into the table, and moved no more. In the sudden silence the sounds of the fight were magnified many times over. I looked at the shopkeeper. Oh, I was really in for it now. Attacking a cop was one of those old-fashioned criminal offences that could now earn you life in prison. And as surprising as it might sound, I didn't want to spend my life in prison. It was really ironic how I, the dangerous criminal, was on the loose while my friends were all on the inside for something simple like texting while driving. At their case, the prosecution had said it was the singular worst case of texting and driving he had ever seen. He had looked down for five whole seconds. Now, we can't have that, now can we? Anything but texting and driving. Six months minimum was handed down. It would definitely be way more in my case. The shopkeeper stared at me as if I had just murdered his mom. I hesitated. He'd seen me. "Sorry about the damage," I said to the shopkeeper. He shook his head instantly. "No, it's nothing! Don't worry about it, man." I saw that he looked absolutely terrified. Heh, being a criminal was fun. When you've done something to deserve life imprisonment anything goes. So I screwed up my mouth, put on my best gangster face, and snarled, "If you say anything, I'll be back, and there'll be no more second fucking chances. Now is that clear, amigo?" He nodded quickly. I strolled out of the shop. There wasn't much time to lose. Every citizen of the US had a contigency plan for moments like these. You never knew when you were going to be arrested, and hovercar getaways were exclusively reserved for the 0.001. Mine was to go to the end of this street. Could I get there? I saw another officer approaching, and quickly I ducked into a side street. There were two thirteen-year old boys - possibly brothers - hiding out there, and they both jumped back in surprise. "You Before they could say a word, I lunged for them, and put one hand on either mouth. "Now listen to me, you cocksuckers, " I said. The swear had the desired effect - their eyes bulged. Both of them now knew they were dealing with a proper criminal. "Don't say a word to the police. I'm going to need your help to get away. You boys heard of a getaway plan? Nod for yes or shake for no." They both nodded. Now came the part that was complete bullshit. "You're going to help me, or I'll kill you two." Hearing this, they struggled a bit, but I had them both under control. Quickly, their shakings subsided. "But I won't, if you help me. Will you help me?" Two nods. I released them both. "Very well. There's a policeman out there and I want one of you to be a decoy. The other person will come with me to the end of the road. If we meet someone else on the way, I'm your father and I'm taking you to see the execution, alright?" They both nodded a third time. "Alright, let's get going," I said. "Won't want to miss when a judge is shot dead, now won't we?" One of them was already moving. Seeing the police officer through the side street, I took a deep breath. This was either going to work or fail spectacularly. Would there be more? - The first inkling that the officer got of trouble came from the boy's screech. "Stop!" the officer said. "You are wanted for truancy!" I pushed the other boy ahead of me. "Walk," I said. "Your brother will join us." That was the second lie. I had no idea what would happen for his brother. Did it matter? The boy was walking ahead of me. The policeman was looking the other way, chasing the screams of a thirteen year old boy who was running for his brother's life. Such was life for the few free citizens in the land of the free. What could possibly go wrong? I reached the end of the road without incident. There was an abandoned shop on the corner. I could see my grab bag in there. A gun peeked out of the top. Hey, at least the prison lobbyists left the Second Amendment untouched. I got over and stuffed the weapon deeper into the bag, before I noticed that the boy was still standing there. "What?" I asked, playing the part. "What're you still doing here? Scram!" "Did you..... did you say there was going to be an execution?" I shouldered my pack. "Yeah, Chief Justice of some sort. Why?" He didn't say anything. I looked at him, saw how well his face matched his brother's. In my head I was already rehearsing my story to the Canadian border force. And then I looked at the boy again, and it hit me. "Oh, no, no..... he's not your father, now is he?" The boy was silent. I sighed, knowing now that there was no choice. The boy had saved my life. Canada could wait. "Right, let's go," I said. "We're going to save your dad."

article: I sit in the cafe sipping my hot chocolate calmly. My entire body aches from running for so long. I look to the window keeping alert. I would have to leave soon and head to the train station; Charlie was the smartest cop that I knew and in all likelihood he was already on my trail. I throw out the cup and grab my backpack ready to go. I look at the train time schedule once I get to the station and deliberate my destination. The secret to being on the run was never having a set plan. If I didn't know where I was going, neither would anyone else. I decide to head upstate towards the countryside; although farming communities were often tightly knit, there were fewer cops and they seemed to be less suspicious than those in the city. I sit on the train and read a magazine. I sense someone sit next to me but I'm too tired to care. I imagine a cozy queen sized bed with tons of pillows that I have to just myself and yawn. The person next to me chuckles and exclaims, " Crime is tiring, huh? " I look up worriedly to see Charlie sitting next to me. He snaps a set of handcuffs one on my wrist and one on the seat. I look around fearfully and he laughs. " There is no one here. I'm not even on duty. We'll get off at the first stop and I'll call in some back up, " he says in an amused tone. I roll my eyes, " Please Charlie, you have to let me go, " I plead. He looks at me disgusted, " You are a murderer, you deserve to be punished, " he says. I shake my head frustrated; I couldn't tell him the truth because he would never believe it. I imagine my " victim's " face. She has short black hair and rosy cheeks, I'm sure she was happy wherever she was. She was only nineteen when she murdered Charlie. After his death, I received a small button in the mail which said, " Press to go back in time ." I pressed it and when she was born, I stole her from the hospital and I left her at a random police station in South Carolina. I figured that she would be put in the foster care system and adopted. I hoped she'd have a better chance with new parents and at the very least I figured that dropping her off so far away would protect Charlie. I couldn't tell anyone or she would be tracked down and returned to her parents doomed to make the same mistakes. Everyone assumed I murdered the baby because she was still missing after all this time and while it sucked, the first time losing Charlie was painful enough; I wasn't going to let it happen again. I look at Charlie and then close my eyes; I was tired of running. " Why did you do it? " he asks quietly. I laugh and answer, " She's not dead. She's just adopted. " He was never going to believe a word out of my mouth. The News had painted me as a maniacal baby killer and my story wasn't exactly the most rational. " Where is she? " he asks picking up my backpack and beginning to go through it. I blush wondering what he'll pull out. I shake my head, " It doesn't matter, " I reply as he pulls out my scrapbook. ' Well this was going to be interesting'I think as he begins to flip through the pages. He wears a puzzled face and says, " You look very nice in these wedding pictures, what happened to your husband? " I smile; of course Charlie would see a picture of himself and think it was someone else. " He died, " I say quietly looking at Charlie's young inquisitive face focused on my scrapbook. He closes the book and puts it back in my bag, " I'm sorry for your loss. Hopefully you'll be able to plead insanity or land in an institution where you can get proper help to cope. " I begin to feel tears in my eyes and look at the handcuff, " Can I go to the bathroom? " I ask. Charlie shakes his head and replies, " Nope. " He was a good cop and wasn't easily fooled. Escaping in the bathroom would be a disgrace for him; I don't think he'd ever forgive himself for that mistake. I wipe my eyes with my free hand and he hands me a tissue. Even when dealing with what he believed was a murderer, he was never cruel. I begin to hyperventilate with worry and he looks at me concerned. " Take a deep breath and just relax. Everything is going to be okay, " he says softly. Charlie had anxiety too and sympathized with anyone who suffered through it as well. I cough and try to distract myself by thinking of good memories. " Can I tie up my hair? " I ask quietly as my tears act as glue between my hair and my face. He looks at me suspiciously and sighs before tying up my hair himself. I chuckle, " You must hate me, " I say. He shakes his head and replies, " You're just sick. You're not evil. " He unlocks the handcuff and grabs my arm tightly. He escorts me off the train and we head to the front of the station. He calls for back up on his cell phone and they arrive within fifteen minutes. A rookie officer puts me in real handcuffs and reads me my rights before leading me to his squad car. I get the feeling that he is very new to the squad from how loose the handcuffs are. I lean against the car tiredly and I hear, " Officer Wilds! " The rookie looks at me curiously and tells me to wait before running over to the older officer. I look around and see that Charlie is being interviewed by two other officers and a lieutenant talking to the rookie. I walk to the front of the car and slip out of the extremely loose handcuffs. I grab my backpack and slip away into an alley way with a smile. I was still tired but at least I wouldn't be sleeping in a cell.

article: "This is never going to sell." Thomas Jefferson Carter, owner and lead editor at Herald Publishing, set his half-sipped gin and tonic on the desk and shoved the manuscript towards me as if the words themselves stunk. Literally. The grandfather clock ticked dutifully. I waited twelve ticks before speaking. "Why not?" "Some of this technology..... it seems far-fetched. Touching pieces of glasses and having images and words come up on them..... books read from some sort of electric library, telegraphs appearing in the palm of your hand, being able not only to speak to but SEE another man from anywhere in the world..." "How is it more far-fetched than Wells or Verne? Than time travel or journeying to the center of the earth?" Carter mumbled to himself, his lips squashing his knee-jerk replies into mush while he chose his answer. "In your story, it seems as if humanity is more connected than ever before, and yet they waste it." " 'T is the definition of'dystopia', sir." Carter's eyes hardened. Once more my wit had outrun my wisdom. "Your story proclaims that we will use all of this achievement for nothing but self-gratifcation. We will use these instant telegraphs to argue with each other over the latest showtunes or the proper length of a woman's skirt. We will not use these portable..... what did you call them?" "Tablets." "We will not use these tablets like Moses did, to carry down the inspiration of God or show a divine truth. We won't even use them to show the greatest wonders of the world to every curious child. In your story, we use them to print pictures of ourselves, to challenge each other to tedious bouts of bantering or to pointless little competitions. It's as if..... these people have no real problems." "Why would there be, sir? You've read the papers, seen the newsreels. They're calling it "the War to end all Wars" over there in Europe. After they're done shelling each other into paste, humanity's taste for blood might finally be sated. Then what will we argue about? Once we see mankind for what it is, one people with the same hopes and dreams and fears, then what is left to divide us?" Carter's chair squeaked as he leaned forward. "So you're saying we make our own problems because all the true problems have been solved?" "I am." The grandfather clock ticked thirteen times. "It's as if your story is a utopian one wrapped up in dystopia. Humanity's greatest achievements will bring about it's greatest boredom." "I like to see myself as a optimistic cynic, sir." He took another sip of his drink and considered the manuscript again. He touched the edge of it, testing to see if, as a result of our conversation, the pages had turned to gold. "No, it'll still never sell. Try again."

article: Brian Lindale cursed at his wife's dogs, like he did every day. Except this time, when he told the purebred Yorkshire terrier to "Die like the rat you are," he meant it. He could deal with the smell they built up over spending hours in their kennels, or the 2am barking that would spark the others to echo that sharp yipping. He even managed to somehow forgive when the smallest one chewed through the power cables on his 66" flat screen television, right when he really needed to just sit and watch something distracting for an hour. But now, images of drowning the animals in their swimming pool were tempted to stay in his mind's eye. Hell, he'd even bury them afterwards, which would be more then they deserve. He hated them especially today because now instead of leaving the house five minutes early, he would be leaving just on time. He checked the clock on his phone. 7:00. Takes twenty minutes to get there, interviews at 7:30. I'll be fine he hoped. Brian carried their kennels to the back door and opened their little gates. He gagged at the smell, and realizing that there was shit even on the handles. He rushed to the kitchen sink to wash his hands immediately, using too much dish soap as he always did. Brian was the type of person who liked clean hands, and if they were ever dirty at some point in the day, he would feel anxious. And even worse, Brian bit his nails down to the flesh, so he had to be extra careful to avoid situations like these. Scrubbing that bit of brown on his hand that just wouldn't come off, he looked up to find the dogs playing with each other, covering their white fur with shit and piss. He looked over to his phone. It showed only a black screen. Brian nudged the front button with his elbow and it showed 7:03. Ill be fine He stepped over the kennels to get to the backyard, careful not to swing the door open too much so the little rats couldn't scurry inside. He scolded them as they tried to jump on his legs. "Shoo, you little shits. Get the fuck away from me." He managed to get to the side of the house, walking barefoot over their white rock landscaping, peppered with bits of dry dog shit. He evaded them all and got to the green hose the gardeners used to water their four palm trees. He traced the hose to its source and turned the spout. He held the hose up, and chilling cold water dribbled out from the tip. He held his thumb on it, but there wasn't enough pressure to make a spray. Brian had to trace the hose again to find where it had folded, and found it on the third try. The pressure inside the hose finally let out, spraying water straight into the air. Now he had dirty water on him, but he didn't care. After this, he would need to shower again anyway. He held his thumb to the tip and sprayed the hose water at the dogs. Of course, they took him for playing and tried to jump at him. If his wife saw him repelling the little rats now by spraying directly into their faces, she would be livid. They misbehave because they know you hate them! she would say. It was the kind of thing that he thought was cute when she said it, but thinking on it later would just irritate him. What kind of sense does that make? Shitting on yourself must be some protest When finally they were as white as their innocent little souls, Brian ushered them into their spare kennels. Of course, the last one never wanted to go back in once he had been let out. But like Brian, we don't all get what we want. He carried their now full kennels inside, trying not to let their yipping get on his nerves. He set them down, walked back to the kitchen sink and checked his phone. 7:08. I'll be fine The shower was nice, at least. He liked his showers hot enough to fog the mirrors. But he didn't have the time to stew in it long. He jumped out, toweled off and slipped into his extra suit. As he walked out the door, he checked his phone. 7:15 If I hurry, I'l be fine Brian powered on his GPS device, and waited anxiously for his directions. Suddenly the screen went dark. Dead? No not now He pressed the power button desperately, but nothing else happened. "Damn NSA" he said aloud. The National Security Agency years ago made a deal with global phone providers to record all audio around every cellular device, and to shut down phones before all power was depleted in order to maintain recording. At least, that's what he had heard. He cursed the NSA out of habit, but also to try and make light of this awful situation. Brian certainly remembered where he was going: for a job interview at the local paper to write a sports column. The press factory for the Reno Times was the largest building in town, outside of North Virgiinia Street. Damn near every schoolboy in the city worked as their paperboys back in the 60s, when he grew up. Times were simpler then. Dogs stayed outside, phones didn't die and employers understood if you had a bad morning coming in. But now, companies just dont care. With one of every seven people unemployed, the companies could be as hard as they wanted on their workers. What would they do, quit? Good luck feeding your family. It was a kind of leverage that would be called criminal, back when Brian grew up. Now it's just good business. He checked his phone again to check the time. Still dead. No idea how late I am Nervously he looked at his hand, and found the nail on his right pinky finger just a bit longer than the others, showing the tiniest sliver of white at the tip. He bit down, remembered his cleaning work that morning, and gagged. He spat outside his window. Best not to think about it. Think about the road, we got ta hurry on Brian backed out of the driveway and went. The kids were on summer break, so there wouldn't be any pedestrians running about trying to catch busses or chase playballs. He remembered almost hitting a child while he was checking his phone for the time. He remembered the panic, a kind of trance you enter where everything can go wrong and your mouth tastes like metal. But seeing no pedestrians around, he sped out of his home. While driving, you always believe you're hitting every red light. Like a man in a traffic control tower is looking at you, making sure the yellow light comes on just far enough away to make you doubt yourself. But now he was certain of it. Brian passed by Piggy Pete's Coffee, which was really just a donut shop with week old coffee. This was the type of place that stayed open until 11pm so the city's hipsters could eat donuts snobbily, if that were a thing. He remembered being a kind of social rebel back then, insisting that his friends listen to the Stones instead of the Beatles, and before that Beatles instead of Elvis. But only the young have time for that now, and certainly not Brian. Traffic slowed to a crawl, and Brian cursed aloud. "Are you fucking kidding me, what now?" He nudged his car to the right so he could look ahead. A quarter mile ahead, on the side of the road, a red minivan had sideswiped a green honda. It was always the green hondas. It's like people who can't drive gravitate to cheap cars they can use up and throw away. But what bothered Brian was that everyone wanted to slow and see what was going on. He wasn't the kind to nose into other people's business, especially one so boring as a traffic accident. But sure enough, every single person driving by bneeded to slow and inspect it. And once they had, they revved up to meet the normal Reno driving speed: Speed Limit 10. article: It smells like cigarettes. It always does in here. Nobody has smoked in here for years, but it's not an odor that time can easily erase. Something about the smel and dim lighting is soothing; refreshing, even. The only feature of the otherwise non-descript watering hole that is McNally's Irish pub, is the lack of features. Along the glossy downtown strip, it's a shadow, creeping across the face of glamour. No neon lights, no Happy Hour specials posted on the door. Just a relic from a former era when a bar was a bar. A place where relics, like myself, can come and drink to remember a time where things were simple and life was slower. No Facespace or Instatweet. Just a cold scotch and colder memories. Familiar faces with stories that are told through a series of nods and grunts. After a particularly Mondayish Thursday, I could think of no place I'd rather be than my stool at the end of the bar with 4 fingers of Powers Irish Whiskey and a pint of Budweiser. Grand dad used to call it a Polish High ball. I call it the usual. I open the door and get greeting by the sweet smell of familiarity. Tip my hat to Morgan behind the bar as I take my usual seat. By the time I've got my hat off and I'm settled in my seat, Morgan has the usual ready to do. I take a moment to remember my grand dad before I drain my whiskey. "Na zdrowie to you, Old Man." I say to myself. Unconsciouly, really. Every first round is for my Grand Dad. Before I can sit back and enjoy the quiet ramblings of Morgan's latest rounds of complaints about his neighbors (The club next to his bar is, apparently, the beginning of the end), I see her. Her. By the very gender of the word, it's cause for confusion at McNally's. Not that it's a chauvinists establishment or anything, but it generally doesn't attract ladies like a cocktail lounge or craft brewery might. Hell, Morgan only knows how to pour whisky and the two beer options are Budweiser or Not Budweiser. By the time I realize she's not an illusion, I realize something else: she's crying. Silently. Not making a fuss about it, not crying out for attention. The tears just stream down her face. She looked like the saddest person I've ever seen. Despite every inch of my body protesting, I do the unthinkable. "Uh..miss?" She turns. She's pretty. Plain, but pretty. Even crying. She just looks so damn sad. "Yes?" She has an accent. Eastern Europe? "Uh..I don't mean to bother.." Am I really that bad at this? " ....yes?" Not unpolitely, but cautious. "It's just that..... well you're there..... you just....I just want to make sure you're ok is all." Good Lord I should have kept my mouth shut. She smiles. I think. I didn't wear my glasses. "Oh. Well that's kind of you." Her accent again. Reminds me of my Grand Dad's. Polish? "I suppose I have had better days." She says. Seems private. I like that. "Haven't we all?" I offer. Well, I did my good deed for the day. This lady is ok and I'm free to pretend to be caring about Morgan's next door night club troubles (Music, loud enough to hear all the way in here after midnight. Madness). "Sir?" Shit. "Uh, yeah?" "Who did you toast to?" "What?" "Na zdrowie. It's a polish toast. I don't mean to pry, but I thought I heard you say it?" "Oh..... yea. Yea I suppose I did." I guess that accent was Polish. "Who did you toast to?" She seems geniunely curious. Oh what the hell. "My grand dad. He came from Poland. Years an' years ago. When he was a young man." "You were close with him?" "Well, yea. He taught me most things I know." She's quiet for a beat. Like she's wrestling an idea. I look to Morgan for an interuption. He's too bothered by the younger crowd peering in his windows (Don't even have the decency to dress right....). Crap. Looks like I'm on my own for this one. "He is gone now?" She asks softly. Sadly, even. "Yea. He passed some years ago." "That must have been difficult." "Well, yea." What is she getting at here? " ....I lost someone." Ah. "My condolences. That why you're crying?" "Yes." "Who did you lose?" She takes a deep breath. "My sister." "That's tough." That's when the dam broke. "Tough? Tough?! It's impossible! She wasn't sick or old! She wasn't in an accident! She just died! Dropped dead in her office at work!" She starts sobbing again. Morgan looks like he's just realizing for the first time that there's a woman in his bar. She stops crying long enough to look up and ask me a question. "How? How do I do this? How do you deal with your grand dad? Please tell me. Please. I came here to get drunk and forget. Is that it? Is that how? Is that what you do?" So that's it. She's never been hurt like this before. "No," I tell her as I hold up 2 fingers to Morgan who, desperate to be busy and away from this situation, readies 2 glasses of whisky and 2 pints of Budweiser. "That's not what I do." "Well what then?" She asks. It's desperate. She's looking for anything to help her forget. Morgan brings us 4 glasses; 2 with Powers, 2 Buds. She looks confused. She looks at the drinks as I set hers in front of her and take mine. "What was your sister's name?" " ..... Kasia." She says it almost defensively. "And your name?" "Karolina." I slide her the whiskey. Lifting my glass, I say "Na zdrowie, Kasia." and drain it. With some hesitation, so does she. She's pretty clearly new to shots and whiskey. After a few coughs and sputters, I slide her the beer. She sips it tentatively. "This is how we forget?" "No, Karolina, this is how we remember." She looks confused. I sip my beer and get comfortable. "Tell me about your sister." She hesitates, then smiles, and I know that it's going to be a long night, but it'll be worth it because she'll be ok and she'll learn how to deal with her first real life scar. Just like Grand Dad tought me.

article: I know that literacy is important, but I'm not sure that just reading books for fun provides any significant benefits for literate adults that other forms of recreation don't. As I understand, the more you use your brain for a particular task, the better you become at that task. That would explain why, when we're really young, parents, teachers, American Library Association posters, etc. encourage us to read books. However, the notion that reading is a healthier, more mentally stimulating activity than playing video games or watching TV seems to persist well into adulthood, when most people are already literate. And that's what confuses me. Reading Harry Potter isn't going to make me better at anything that matters (e.g., math), and neither will reading, say, Ulysses. If I'm not going to study or worki.e., if I'm just killing timeI don't think it makes a difference whether I read a book (regardless of how challenging or culturally significant it is) or play Battlefield 4. I've been thinking about this, because, if you ever visit any of the subreddits dedicated to productivity or motivation, such as rGetMotivated, rGetDisciplined, etc., they'll tell you that gaming is a bad habit, or at least a habit that needs to be kept under control. article: Ethan couldn't wait to try out the game - from what he'd seen of the trailers, the graphics were eerily realistic. Though Sims 4 had been good, it had never been quite realistic enough for him. When he got home and popped in the CD, he began jotting out his plans for his first family. He couldn't wait to get started. He built the house carefully: a pool surrounding them, a nice, roomy basement. A family of eight, six of them children. At first, it was the same as usual. His sims' needs plummeted as he deprived them of food and sleep. It was fun, but not exactly anything new. It was only when they started working together on their own, to escape the basement, that he begun to wonder. This wasn't supposed to happen. One of the drawbacks of the game - they were just stupid, simulated people, doing exactly what he told them. Not like real people. Real people would act like this, would try to escape. His hands trembled with excitement as he tried to direct them. Some - like the smallest children - obeyed, while others appeared to be screaming directly at him. One of the parents refused to attack his own children like he'd ordered, instead breaking down in tears on the floor. There could only be one explanation. " You're all real, aren't you? You're real, " he whispered, leaning back from the computer as he considered the implications of this. If they were real, did that mean he was God? He'd always suspected, but this was surely a sign...a signal. He turned his eyes on the sims again. Feverishly, lost in the dark world he had been afraid to imagine up to this point, he began to play in earnest. - " I've got something, sir, " agent Katherine Masters said, showing her supervisor the live feed of one of the webcams. A pale-faced young man's eyes were lit with joy as he tortured a family of eight. " Good job, Katherine, " agent Daniel Simmons murmured, hastening over to check the feed for himself. As always, he felt slightly nauseous as he watched the man's enraptured expression. Right from the start, the Sadism Identification Mechanism operation had been a massive pain in the ass to get approved and implemented. First there was the game's development. It had been a long, tedious slog, to get the coding perfect - to make the sims behave as unpredictably as possible. Then the marketing - its number of sales were crucial to their operation's success. And above all, getting approval to hack into the players'webcams. It would be a disaster if details of the operation became public, even though they abandoned most of the feeds after a week. Watching someone direct their sims to go to work and make pancakes was hardly a good use of their resources. But then there were others. The ones who made the red tape and headaches worth it. The ones who proved that the game could be a revolutionary tool to catch some perpetrators early. Those who would likely move on from torturing highly realistic, simulated people - to real people. " You've got the address? " he asked. " All his details, " Katherine confirmed. " Keep watching him, " Daniel said. " We need more." Katherine started to reply, when they heard Ethan whisper something in a fervent tone, like he was praying. " You're all real, aren't you? You're real, " he said. Instead of seeming uneasy, the boy looked ecstatic. " Delusions, " Daniel noted. " Interesting. Focus only on him for now, Katherine. " She nodded, stifling a sigh. It was draining work, looking into these people's eyes when they thought no-one was watching. It had already been a pain with the previous games. But somehow, the things she saw only got worse as the games got more realistic. People got increasingly carried away as they dreamt they could control actual people. "Yesss! I'm God!" Ethan was whispering to himself as he drowned two of his sims in the pool, while another was consumed by flames in the kitchen. Katherine made a note of that, shaking her head as she took a sip of coffee. The number of people who immediately jumped to that conclusion was rather disturbing. Hope you enjoyed my story! Your body regulates your body temperature in cool conditions by constantly moving the blood within your skin. If the blood doesn't circulate fast enough, it will cool and cause you to feel cold. That's why moving around when it's cold outside can help to keep you warm. Your heart beats faster, so blood doesn't stay near the surface of your skin as long. There is a constant supply of warm blood moving from the center of your body outward, while the cool blood moves back to the center of your body and is warmed up. article: Just today, I saw mention of a story that some lawyer named Larry Klayman is attempting to have President Barack Obama deported due to his perceived lack of citizenship. This hearkens back to the "birther" movement, and all of the conservatives who have some mistaken conception that our president wasn't actually born in Hawaii, and therefore is not a US citizen, and is therefore not eligible to hold office. Aside from that, however, it got me to wondering - what would it matter if that were true? What if Obama were born in Kenya, then moved to the United States at a very young age, was raised here, and lived his life working towards becoming a public servant and eventually president? Is there any indication that he's not fulfilled his obligations in the exact same way as someone who was physically born in the US, instead of some East African nation? Which brought me back to something I've thought about before: Why do we still cling to Article II, Section 1, Clause 5 of the US Constitution, which stipulates that the president must be a natural-born citizen of the United States? I understand its importance in a historical context - as a fledgling nation, we needed to be assured of the patriotism of any potential Chief Executive. But in the 21st century, the United States is a much more variegated population, and we've already seen some prominent politicians who wouldn't qualify to serve as president based on that strict standard, such as Arnold Schwarzenegger, or one of my favorites, former Michigan governor Jennifer Granholm. So, I believe it's time to revisit this section of the Constitution, and amend it to include naturalized citizens. We can leave in the part that requires a 14 year residence, or even increase it, if we're that concerned, but I think following a dedicated leader who has lived in this country long enough to be interested in serving it in a fairly thankless job is proof enough that they wouldn't abuse the position to unduly serve their birth nation instead. article: There are several kinds of microphones. The most basic is called a "dynamic" microphone. It works by having a large coil of wire move around a magnet, which induces a voltage in the coil that then becomes the audio signal. Dynamic microphones are generally durable and can handle high sound pressure levels, making them suitable for live performances and recording in loud environments. There are also "condenser" microphones, which use a capacitor to capture sound. Condenser microphones are more sensitive and have a wider frequency response than dynamic microphones, making them suitable for capturing detailed audio in quieter environments. However, they are generally more fragile and require a power source to operate. Another type of microphone is the "ribbon" microphone, which uses a thin strip of metal suspended between magnets to capture sound. Ribbon microphones have a distinct character and warmth to their sound, but they are also extremely delicate and sensitive to the environment around them. Finally, there are also specialized microphones such as lavalier microphones that can be clipped onto clothing, and shotgun microphones that can be mounted on a camera to capture directional audio from a distance. The type of microphone you choose will depend on the environment you plan to record in and the type of audio you want to capture.

article: My own perspective is British, but this is something I'm seeing crop up in many European countries. The topic of immigration is possibly the most popular debate going on right now. In the U.K, immigration is consistently in the papers, our leaders are continually speaking about it, and it is always discussed on political shows such as Question Time. It's become so popular that we have elected UKIP, a right-wing party who advocates strong immigration policy, as our European representative, not to mention their continued growth in successful elections around the country. The rise of right wing parties advocating stronger immigration control can be seen in many other countries - France, Germany, Spain etc, and these parties are all gaining popularity. Firstly, I think that as we live in Democracy, the will of the people must be heard. If immigration is consistently polling as the number 1 issue people want changing, if the rise of stricter immigration policy parties continue, and if people continue to protest (as shown in Germany recently), the issue must be adressed by government. I feel that isn't particularly the case. If we look to Germany recently - the protest was organized by very shady people, but the elected officials immediately branded those whom worry about immigration as in the same boat as the 'nazis in pinstripes' who organized the protest. Look at the recent comments made in France - people who worry about immigration are 'spiteful'. There's a continued backlash in many of these countries by the elected, which is often presented in ways similar to above - evoke themes of racism, patriotism (often seen as a dirty word in Europe), xenophobia in relation to anti-immigration worries in an effort to simply brush it away. If we take an extreme example - Look at sweden. The fear to criticize immigration is so strong that there are numerous examples where when newspapers report on crimes committed by immigrants - the blurred out, anonymized photos they use in their articles are actually whitewashed. As in, made to look as if the immigrants are from European descent. Sweden simply refuses to have any form of discussion on the issue. Not only do I find this problematic (and wonder if these parties are beginning to rely on an immigrant vote - sort of how the left in the US relies on the hispanic black vote), I feel it's counterproductive. When the government brushes aside these valid concerns, the populous who do worry will feel embittered and turn to their only remaining solution - these right wing parties. So, my first two points are - that, as a democracy, the will of people must be adressed, and that the popularity of the issue and the rise of certain political parties across the european spectrum highlight how much of an issue this is. Further, there's a fear by politicians to adress these concerns, whether they be it simply for being labelled as racist or for some other reason, and that some politicians conversely use the labels just mentioned to actively shut down discussion. article: It's about a 10 difference, with the troy ounce (31.1 grams) being heavier than the avoirdupois ounce (standard ounce, 28.35 grams). However, a troy pound (12 troy ounces) is lighter than a standard pound (16 ounces). There was this market place in France, in the city of Troyes, where people came from all around the world to trade. The word probably derives from that market, where they developed a system of measurement that could be used so that all the goods in the market place was the same. That way, no one could be cheated based on the weight of their goods being calculated differently. The system was probably derived from an older system developed by the Romans, where the "pound" was called "aes grave," and the "ounce" was "uncia," defined as 112th of an aes grave. Hence the troy pound being comprised of 12 troy ounces instead of the usual 16 ounces. The avoirdupois ounce is the full name for the standard ounce that we use in everyday measurements. All the stuff at your local grocery store is measured in avoirdupois ounces, your bathroom scale is set that way, the entire Imperial system of measurement uses it. You've probably never heard the full name because we generally just call it "ounces.,'The Troy ounce is a traditional unit of gold weight. (31.1 g) The ounce is used for everything else. (28.35 g)

article: Depends on what you mean by "permanently." If you just told your operating system to delete a file, it's not permanently deleted. The data is not erased. Nor is it moved. Nothing happens to it at all. There's just no longer a marker in the table-of-content saying "There's a file on page 17." If you permanently delete a file, the implication (to an IT expert) is that you've gone out of your way to make sure that data is not there any more. As in, you used a program that actually goes to where that file's data was and overwrites it quite a few times using random data, as well as marking it as no longer there.','On a normal hard drive, files are not actually deleted when you "delete it permanently." What happens is that area of the hard drive where the file resided is no longer listed as the file in the file system, meaning that another file can overwrite that area. But before this, the data is still there and can be recovered using software. On all modern SSDs on a modern OS, things are handled differently. Due to how flash storage functions, simply marking the area of a deleted file as free space and leaving the data there degrades write speed as the drive fills with and writes over deleted data. So modern OSes have what's called a TRIM command. As soon as a file is deleted on an SSD, that space is immediately overwritten with zeroes.', "They don't actually get moved anywhere else or deleted, they are just no longer marked as anything, so when you go to save something else later on it can be saved over the top of what you have deleted, that's why sometimes it's possible to rescue deleted files, because nothing has replaced them yet

article: They aren't powers of 360. They are multiples of 360. A power of 360 would be represented as 360720," "It makes scaling between them simpler. For some time, for the sake of backwards-compatibility, it's best to scale old content up rather than re-master it. Think of a tiny picture with 2x2 pixels. And two new displays with 3x3 pixels and 4x4 pixels. To scale the image up to the 4x4 display is simple enough. Just repeat each pixel twice. But the 3x3 will be a pain. If you repeat the first pixel, but not the second since you can't, the image will stay sharp but distort. If you count the average from neighboring pixels and fill the extra pixels with that, the image won't distort but won't be sharp either. Or you can keep the 2x2 image and fill the rest with black bars. A 5x5 display would similarly sucks but 6x6 would be sweet again. I'm only using small numbers to make up a worst-case scenario. It all kind of blends in the mass when the resolutions are in the thousands. But it's still noticeable. To see what I mean in real-life, for a distorted image, try setting a 4:3 resolution in your 16:9 monitor. Everything will stretch wider. And for blurry image, try setting a resolution that's close to your display's native resolution but not exactly it. For example 1050p for 1080p display. Depending on how your monitor handles things, it may add the black bars or do the averaging thing. These you are more likely to find in-OS. On third-party applications that allow custom resolutions, it's possible to find even better (or worse) examples. So to scale up a 720p image to 1080p they have the option of repeating every other pixel. It's not optimal, but keeps the image similar enough. Same goes for 1080p to 1440p. from 1080p to 4k it's again repeating every pixel. From 720p to 1440p it's repeating every pixels. And of course, if the content is specially made for 1440p or 4k, it'll be pristine on those displays and to scale down to 1080p or 720p, they leave out pixels.,Modern Computer resolutions inherited their display sizes from a legacy of punch cards and the number of scan lines of cathode ray tubes. You see the original graphics resolution for PCs was VGA with 640x480 and most of the ones that came later like like SVGA (800x600) were based upon that. The VGA inherited the resolution from text based resolution where you did not display graphics but rather charters in for example an 80 by 25 or 80 by 60 grid. If you have an 80x60 grid and use 8by8 pixels per character you arrive at the original VGA resolution. The 80s characters per line is something far older that modern computer displays. IBM standardized on punch cards with 80 columns in 1928. So the whole 80 characters was sort of inherited from those type of equipment (also 72 characters were often used with teletypes for practical reasons.) This sort of gave you the horizontal resolution increments we still use to day. The vertical ones from your question came thanks to the combination of wanting nice square characters that were 8x8 pixels in the beginning and the whole thing being compatible with American TV screens which were based on NTSC which had 480 scan-lines. Early home computers used TVs as their display. So that was the limit they could use. Originally TVs were not digital like today but analogue. They did not have any pixels just a ray of electrons that wandered back and forth and down from the bottom across as specially made glass surface making it glow. Horizontally they theoretically did not have any resolution at all, but vertically it was divided into rows upon rows that they ray moved along. article: The way I see it, no one is there on their own accord. You weren't asked if you wanted to be born - you were simply roped into living. There is also no contractual obligation for you to stay (read: there is no obligation for anyone to stay alive.) The way I see it, there's two sides, A (the world, society, family, etc) and B (given individual): A brings B in without asking, wants B to stay (as seen by all the anti-suicide arguments) B is not here on their own accord, and ergo has no reason to stay by default. Therefore it is up to A to convince B to stay. A good analogy is getting a pet. You get a kitten because you want a kitten. When the kitten grows up, you keep feeding and caring for it, so that it has a reason not to run away. However, this isn't the case for A and B. The situation that's actually present makes no sense. Here's how it is: A wants B to stay. B does not have a reason to stay. However, A is not interested in providing for B if B doesn't work. A will not give anything to B, unless B works for A. So, it's a bit like dragging someone to a restaurant and expecting them to cook the food and pay the bill - all while expecting B to remain complacent and agreeable. If we transpose it to real life, we effectively have societylife, who wishes for X individual to stay (by making suicide either illegal, or immoral, or wrong). However, societylife does nothing for X individual unless X does something first. Oftentimes, X will be expected to work for societylife without societylife giving anything back. "Weird," I thought to myself, "Ever since the TTIP had been passed people had been acting..... malicious." I shook my head and kept walking. I knew what this was - They knew what this was. That was my house on fire. With this large of a crowd here, it was evident what had happened. It was a siren's song that she couldn't ignore, and so she set her mind to do something she hadn't done in years make a new friend. The ancient swing creaked above Ray as he gently thrust his legs back and forth in a mindless, autonomous motion. After school, he would always venture to the local playground near his house to sit on the swing set and play his Game Boy while his stacks of undone homework practically pushed a hole through the hypothetical ceiling. The bottom of his shoes brushed against he chips of wood or whatever they were below him. He was too distracted by his game to give it much thought, but his subconscious couldn't help but remember a time when his tiny, kindergarten feet didn't even reach the ground on that very swing. Ray was a creature of habit. For as long as he could remember, he had been going to the same park, sitting on the same swing, pattering away at the buttons of the same Game Boy. He remembered a time when he wasn't the biggest kid at the park, when other kids his age would actually sit next to him on the swing set.
